name: The Blood Lord
tagline: Stack haemorrhage until enemies delete themselves, then do it again.
fantasy: You do not out-damage anything. You fill a hidden bar on your target, and when it fills the game rips a chunk out of their health bar for you. Every katana swing, every dagger flick, every swarm of flies is a deposit into that bar, and the payout does not care how much armour the thing in front of you is wearing.

route.text: Start as Bandit with Great Knife - the class begins with it; 38 base bleed and a 1.5 weight makes it your opening bleed stick.
Get Reduvia - beat Bloody Finger Nerijus, who invades in the riverbed under the bridge beside Murkwater Cave.
Get Uchigatana - Deathtouched Catacombs in northern Limgrave, on a ledge reached through an illusory wall by the first staircase.
Get Ash of War: Bloody Slash - dropped by the Bloodcrazed Godrick Knight at Fort Haight in the east.
Get Crimsonburst Crystal Tear - the Erdtree Avatar guarding the Minor Erdtree; it drips 7 HP a second for three minutes.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gatehouse above Stormhill; a Blood-affinity dagger already shortens this fight badly.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the throne room at the top of Stormveil Castle; you want to be near level 40 here.
Get Bloodflame Blade - a scarab northwest of Rose Church, the island chapel south of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Get Pureblood Knight's Medal - White Mask Varre at Rose Church hands it over after you take his fingers, win three invasions and soak the Lord of Blood's Favor in maiden's blood.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the Grand Library at the top of the academy; she is also your respec vendor from here on.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the Wailing Dunes, entered through Redmane Castle in the southeast.
Take Black Whetblade - on a corpse beside the altar in Night's Sacred Ground, down the crater Radahn's falling star opens near Fort Haight.
Take Mimic Tear Ashes - a chest sealed behind an imp-statue door in Nokron; one Stonesword Key opens it.
Take Radagon's Soreseal - Fort Faroth in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, among the rats in the barn you drop into from the roof.
Take Nagakiba - lying on the ground beside Bloody Finger Hunter Yura at the Second Church of Marika, after you have helped him in Limgrave and Liurnia.
Get Eleonora's Poleblade - Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger invades at that same church the moment Yura's story ends.
Get Bloody Helice - the cellar chest at Writheblood Ruins, north of the Second Church of Marika.
Get Lord of Blood's Exultation - Esgar, Priest of Blood, in the Leyndell Catacombs inside the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds; this is the single biggest damage jump in the guide.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the Erdtree Sanctuary at the summit of the capital; level 80 is a comfortable number to arrive with.
Take White Mask - one of the three Nameless White Mask invaders wading the blood lake of Mohgwyn Palace, northwest of the Palace Approach Ledge-Road grace; the medal warps you straight in.
Take Swarm of Flies - a corpse at the end of a cave in the northeastern quarter of that same blood lake.
Get Ash of War: Blood Tax - a scarab north of the Palace Approach Ledge-Road grace.
Beat Mohg, Lord of Blood - the Dynasty Mausoleum at the bottom of the palace; beating him is one of the two demigod kills that unlock the Land of Shadow.
Get Ash of War: Seppuku - an invisible scarab on the northern shore of the frozen lake, near the First Church of Marika.
Get Rivers of Blood - Bloody Finger Okina invades at the entrance to the Church of Repose, west of the Forge of the Giants.
Get Thorny Cracked Tear - the Putrid Avatar at the Minor Erdtree east of Ordina, Liturgical Town.
Get Rotten Winged Sword Insignia - take Millicent's golden summon sign above the rot pool in Elphael and fight her sisters at her side.
Get Shard of Alexander - finish Iron Fist Alexander in the northwest of the city and speak to him where he falls.
Beat Malenia, Blade of Miquella - the lift arena beneath Elphael; bleed is the answer the community settled on for a reason.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the Erdtree's heart; level 125 to 150 is the comfortable finishing range.
Take Backhand Blade - beside a coffin in a small stone building north-northeast of the Scorched Ruins grace, still carrying its Ash of War: Blind Spot.
Take Blade of Mercy - a chest at the top of the Scorched Ruins; +20% attack power for 20 seconds after any critical hit.
Get Bloodfiend's Arm - dropped by one of the bloodfiends prowling Prospect Town.
Get Rakshasa's Great Katana - beat Rakshasa in the Eastern Nameless Mausoleum.

variants.name: The Cutthroat
variants.twist: Drop the katanas entirely and win with two daggers, permanent mobility and the bleed proc doing all the accounting.
variants.notes: Reduvia asks for only 5 Strength, 13 Dexterity and 13 Arcane, so it is online almost from the first hour and never falls off, since its blood loss and its Arcane scaling both keep climbing with your build. Its skill, Reduvia Blood Blade, costs 6 FP and throws a ranged arc of blood that also builds haemorrhage, which turns your dagger into a poke tool against anything you would rather not touch. Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step costs 5 FP and makes you briefly invisible mid-dodge, and it can be put on daggers, so you can carry it on the off-hand blade while the main hand keeps a damage skill. Give one dagger Occult and the other Blood if you want both flavours of scaling; the buildup from either hand feeds the same meter on the target. This variant wants Dexterity a little higher and Arcane a little lower than the main sheet, because dagger swing speed is what fills the meter.

route.text: Get Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step - the Night's Cavalry that patrols the easternmost bridge of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow after dark.

variants.name: The Bloodflame Priest
variants.twist: Spend twelve points of Faith and turn every weapon you own into a bleed weapon, plus a spell that bleeds things you never have to walk up to.
variants.notes: Bloodflame Blade costs 20 FP, takes one memory slot and needs 12 Faith and 10 Arcane. It coats your weapon for 60 seconds so that every hit smears on an effect worth 40 blood loss buildup over the next two seconds, which is buildup you get for free on top of whatever the weapon already applies. Swarm of Flies wants 11 Faith and 16 Arcane, costs 14 FP, and each of its bloodflies carries 150 total buildup, which is why it strips bosses that will not let you stand next to them. Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear is the reward for trading Mohg's remembrance to Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold; it needs 24 Strength one-handed or 16 two-handed alongside 14 Dexterity and 27 Arcane, so the level-150 sheet above can two-hand it exactly. Shard of Alexander raises skill damage by 15%, and since Bloodboon Ritual and Blood Tax are both skills, it is doing more work here than a Soreseal ever could. You give up the Soreseal's free +5 Vigor and Endurance, so lean on the Crimsonburst Crystal Tear to cover the missing health.

variants.name: The Backhand Killer (Shadow of the Erdtree)
variants.twist: Trade reach for the fastest weapon class in the game and let the DLC's critical-hit talisman feed the same buff loop.
variants.notes: The Backhand Blade needs only 10 Strength and 13 Dexterity, weighs 2.0 and takes normal Smithing Stones, which means you can carry two of them and infuse both Occult the moment you have the Black Whetblade. Ash of War: Swift Slash only fits backhand blades, costs 16 FP, and can be charged for a longer forward step, and you get it by answering the golden summon sign on the Shadow Keep battlements to fight beside Hornsent against Needle Knight Leda. Be careful with that one: the sign vanishes if you reach Messmer the Impaler first, so do it on the way in, not on the way back. Blade of Mercy is +20% attack power for 20 seconds after a critical attack, which suits a weapon class built around getting behind people. Remember that inside the Land of Shadow your normal levels barely matter next to your Scadutree Blessing, so pick up shadow-tree fragments constantly.

route.text: Get Ash of War: Swift Slash - the battlements just before the Storehouse, First Floor grace, by taking the golden sign to help Hornsent.

pvp:
Duel-meta invasions cluster at level 125 and 150, and this build is comfortable at either; take the
150 sheet if you want the extra Vigor. Understand that the arena maths change: Lord of Blood's
Exultation falls from +20% to +12%, the White Mask from +10% to +6%, and the bleed proc itself only
takes 15% of a player's maximum health rather than shredding a boss bar. That is still lethal,
which is why Rivers of Blood has the reputation it does, so expect other players to be pre-rolling
Corpse Piler on sight. Corpse Piler is also parryable across all six of its hits, so mix in normal
swings rather than mashing the skill, and remember Rivers of Blood cannot be buffed by Bloodflame
Blade or any grease, so the Bloodflame Priest variant is a purely player-versus-environment idea.
why:
Blood loss is a status effect, which in Elden Ring means an invisible meter that every hit adds
to and that drains back down if you stop hitting. Fill the meter and it "procs": the game applies
a burst of damage that ignores the normal defence maths entirely. The wiki's numbers are the whole
reason this archetype exists. A proc deals a flat amount plus a percentage of the target's maximum
health, and that percentage is 15% on ordinary enemies and players, 10.5% on bosses and the enemies
that fight alongside them. The flat part is normally 100, but it doubles to 200 when the proc came
from a Somber Smithing Stone weapon that has innate blood loss and Arcane scaling. Read that again,
because it is the single sentence that decides your build: the game pays you extra for using
Arcane-scaling bleed weapons specifically.

Arcane is the stat that feeds all of it. Levelling Arcane raises the buildup that Blood, Poison and
Occult weapons apply, so each swing fills the meter faster and the proc arrives sooner. It also
raises Discovery (your item-drop rate) by one point per level, and it props up Holy defence and
Vitality, which is your resistance to instant-death effects. That is a lot of quiet value for a
stat most builds ignore.

The affinity choice is where new players go wrong. Blood affinity adds raw bleed buildup and some
Arcane scaling, and it is the obvious pick. Occult affinity instead converts a weapon to Arcane
scaling on its physical damage while leaving the weapon's own status scaling intact, and it needs
the **Black Whetblade** before you can apply it. For a weapon that already bleeds on its own, Occult
usually wins: you get the doubled flat proc, your physical hits scale off the stat you are already
buying, and your weapon skill keeps its full Arcane scaling instead of the weakened version Blood
affinity leaves behind. Blood affinity is still correct on a weapon with no innate bleed that you
just want to bleed, such as a plain **Great Knife** on the way to something better.

Now the multipliers. **Lord of Blood's Exultation** gives +20% attack power for 20 seconds whenever
anything within about seven metres is bleeding, including the thing you just cut. The **White Mask**
head piece stacks a further +10% off the same trigger. Both drop to +12% and +6% in PvP, which is
still enormous. Add **Millicent's Prosthesis** (+5 Dexterity and up to +11% after a run of
consecutive hits), **Rotten Winged Sword Insignia** (up to +13% on the same idea), and the
**Thorny Cracked Tear** in your flask (up to +20% for 180 seconds from landing hits), and a build
whose base attack rating looks unimpressive on the character sheet ends up hitting like a
colossal weapon while also proccing bleed every few seconds. That is the whole trick: bleed pays
you in health-bar percentage, and the bleed itself turns on your damage buffs.
firstHour:
Pick Bandit, whose level 5 start of 10 Vigor, 11 Mind, 10 Endurance, 9 Strength, 13 Dexterity,
9 Intelligence, 8 Faith and 14 Arcane is the cleanest possible foundation here, and take the
**Great Knife** it hands you out of the tutorial cave. Run past the Tree Sentinel on the road, grab
Torrent from the first grace, and go straight for the riverbed under the bridge near Murkwater Cave,
where Bloody Finger Nerijus invades; kill him for **Reduvia**, which is the entire early game in one
2.5-weight dagger. Take the Uchigatana out of the Deathtouched Catacombs next if you want a second
option with reach. Put Blood affinity on nothing yet, because you cannot until later, and simply
lean on Reduvia's own buildup while you level Vigor to about 20 and Arcane to about 18. Spend
nothing on Intelligence or Faith for now, and do not touch Strength past 12.

name: The Assassin
tagline: Bleed, backstab, vanish - a DEX/ARC killer that ends fights before they start.
fantasy: You are the thing that is already behind the enemy. You open with a knife in the spine, you finish with a red mist that takes a third of a boss health bar in one tick, and when the counterattack comes you are simply not standing there any more. Nothing you do lasts longer than two seconds.

route.text: Beat Soldier of Godrick - the Cave of Knowledge, reached by dropping down from the Stranded Graveyard where the game deposits you.

Get Reduvia - the riverbed under the bridge beside Murkwater Cave; Bloody Finger Nerijus invades the moment you arrive and locks you in, and Bloody Finger Hunter Yura will come to help if you retreat toward the bridge.
Get Uchigatana - Deathtouched Catacombs, west of Saintsbridge in northern Stormhill; the blade waits on a hidden platform with a skeleton archer, just short of the lever.
Get Assassin's Crimson Dagger - a guaranteed drop from the assassin lurking in the farthest chamber of those same catacombs.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the approach to the Stormveil Castle gate. Backstabs only land on him once his stance meter is broken, so save them.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the throne room at the top of Stormveil Castle. You should reach the end of the early act around level 40.
Get Winged Sword Insignia - the floor of Stillwater Cave, from the knight guarding the bottom.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the library at the Academy of Raya Lucaria; from then on she will rebirth your character for a Larval Tear, which is your safety net if you overspent early.
Get Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step - the Night's Cavalry that patrols the easternmost bridge of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow at night, north of Lenne's Rise.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the Wailing Dunes, once the festival at Redmane Castle has opened.
Get Black Whetblade - Night's Sacred Ground, on a corpse beside the altar that overlooks the giant silver tear. Radahn's fall punched the crater near Fort Haight that lets you down here.
Get Mimic Tear Ashes - the chest behind an imp statue that wants a Stonesword Key. It costs 660 health rather than FP, which is the real reason this build keeps investing in Vigor.
Get Ash of War: Blood Blade - an unmarked scarab in the pond south of the Old Altus Tunnel entrance, east of Erdtree-Gazing Hill.
Get Raptor's Black Feathers - a chest behind an illusory wall in Sage's Cave.

Get Nagakiba - the Second Church of Marika, northwest of Altus Highway Junction, where Yura's story runs out; Eleonora invades immediately afterwards and drops Eleonora's Poleblade. Aim to be around level 80 by the close of the mid act.
Get Dagger Talisman - Volcano Manor: from the throne room take the stairs west before the waygate, spend two Stonesword Keys on the imp statue, then cross the catwalks to a dangling corpse.

Get Black Knife Tiche - Ringleader's Evergaol on the northwestern tip of the Moonlight Altar, an area that only opens through Ranni's questline. Her Blade of Death does percentage-based damage, which pairs with your own percentage damage.
Get Lord of Blood's Exultation - Leyndell Catacombs, entered from the crayfish hall south of the Underground Roadside grace in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the Erdtree Sanctuary at the top of the capital.
Get Ash of War: Seppuku - an invisible scarab on the northern shore of the frozen lake, opposite the First Church of Marika. Swing at empty air until something dies.
Get Rivers of Blood - the Church of Repose on the southwestern side of Flame Peak, west of the Forge of the Giants; Bloody Finger Okina invades at the door and it is his guaranteed drop.
Beat Fire Giant - the pass above the Forge of the Giants.

Get White Mask - Mohgwyn Palace, from the masked invader by the giant crow northwest of the Palace Approach Ledge-Road grace. Reach the palace either through the sending gate on the western edge of the Consecrated Snowfield or with the medal White Mask Varre gives you.
Get Shard of Alexander - finish Iron Fist Alexander in the northwest of the ruins and speak to him afterwards; it is +15% on skill damage, which means +15% on every Corpse Piler.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - the Dragon Temple rooftop. Level 125 is a sensible landing point for the end of the late act.

Get Thorny Cracked Tear - the Minor Erdtree east of Ordina, Liturgical Town. The region itself opens when both halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, from the Village of the Albinaurics and from Castle Sol, are used at the Grand Lift of Rold.

Get Rotten Winged Sword Insignia - Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree: answer Millicent's gold summon sign at the Prayer Room and help her cut down her four sisters. Refusing her and using the red sign instead gives Millicent's Prosthesis - five Dexterity and a weaker version of the same curve - so pick one.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the roots at the foot of the Erdtree.

Get Backhand Blade - beside a coffin in a gazebo in the Inquisitor camp, north-northeast of the Scorched Ruins grace. You arrive in the Land of Shadow by touching the withered arm in the Cocoon of the Empyrean in Mohg's arena, which requires Radahn and Mohg both dead.
Get Blade of Mercy - a chest at the top of the Scorched Ruins. It is +20% attack for 20 seconds after any critical attack, and it refreshes on the next one.

Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight - Castle Ensis, on the eastern road out of the plain. Feed every Scadutree Fragment you find to a site of grace before you try her; the blessing has 21 levels and only counts inside the DLC.

Get Bloodsucking Cracked Tear - dropped by the furnace golem stamping around the entrance to the Ruins of Unte. It is +20% damage for 180 seconds at the price of a health tick every second, which suits a build that heals off criticals.
Beat Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent) - the top of Shadow Keep.
Beat Promised Consort Radahn - the Gate of Divinity. Level 150 with a high Scadutree Blessing is the comfortable place to stand here.

variants.name: The Silent Blade
variants.twist: Drop the katana entirely and win with backstabs, ripostes and a knife that hits like a boulder.
variants.notes: The Misericorde has a 140 critical rating, the highest in the game, and it is a regular Smithing Stone weapon so you can stamp Occult on it once you own the Black Whetblade. Stack the Dagger Talisman with the Assassin's Crimson Dagger and the DLC Blade of Mercy, and every successful backstab pays you damage, health and a 20-second attack buff at once. This variant lives or dies on positioning, so Bloodhound's Step goes on the knife rather than Seppuku, which cannot be applied to daggers anyway. Against bosses that never turn their back, break stance with charged heavy attacks and cash in the riposte.

route.text: Get Misericorde - Stormveil Castle, behind a fog wall that costs one Stonesword Key, near the roaming Grafted Scion and the elevator up to Rampart Tower; take this detour before you climb to Godrick's throne room.

variants.name: The Twinblade Bloodhound
variants.twist: Two blades, a fire trail and jump attacks that hemorrhage a whole crowd at once.
variants.notes: Eleonora's Poleblade wants 21 Dexterity and 19 Arcane, carries 55 blood loss at +0 and cannot be infused or buffed, so it is a straight Somber upgrade path with nothing to think about. Its Bloodblade Dance skill costs 11 FP and covers ground, which turns the build from a duellist into a blender. Because a twinblade lands so many hits per swing, the jump attack route pays: the Claw Talisman adds 15% to jump attacks and Raptor's Black Feathers adds another 10% on top, and the wiki notes those two multiply rather than merely add. Find the Claw Talisman on a Stormveil Castle watchtower reached from the Rampart Tower grace, and pick up Erdtree's Favor +2 in Leyndell, Ashen Capital afterwards to carry the extra weight.

variants.name: The Shadow Cutthroat
variants.twist: A Shadow of the Erdtree lane built around backhand blades, self-damage buffs and running attacks.
variants.notes: Backhand blades are a DLC weapon class with a deceptive reach and a Blind Spot skill that steps around a guard for 9 FP. The base Backhand Blade takes affinities, so stamp Blood on it and let your Arcane do the work. Lacerating Crossed-Tree adds 15% to running light and heavy attacks, which is exactly how this weapon class wants to be played, and Needle Knight Leda hands it over at the Highroad Cross grace in Scadu Altus after you back her in the Shadow Keep co-invasion. The Bloodsucking Cracked Tear drains health every second for its 20% damage, so keep the Assassin's Crimson Dagger equipped and treat criticals as your flask. Remember the blessing ceiling: without Scadutree Fragments the Land of Shadow will feel unfairly punishing no matter how good the build is.

pvp: Duel at 125 and invade at 150; both levels leave you with roughly 50 Vigor and enough Dexterity and Arcane to keep the bleed threatening. Blood loss is worth less against people than against monsters - the percentage stays at 15% but human health pools are small, and Lord of Blood's Exultation drops from 20% to 12% while the White Mask drops from 10% to 6%. What actually wins duels is Bloodhound's Step, the invisible frames of which are close to unfair, and the fact that Seppuku pre-buffs your damage before the fight starts. Avoid leaning on critical talismans in PvP: backstabs are hard to earn against a moving player, and the Claw Talisman falls to 7.5% there. Expect Rivers of Blood to be answered with a bleed-resistant setup, and be ready to swap to the Nagakiba, whose extra reach is the least counterable thing you own.
why:
Elden Ring has two ways to kill something: subtract its health one swing at a time, or fill an invisible second meter and make the game subtract a slab of health for you. That second meter is **blood loss**, sometimes called hemorrhage. Every hit from a bleed weapon adds points to a hidden bar on the target. When the bar fills, the bar empties and the target instantly takes a burst of damage: a flat chunk plus a percentage of its own maximum health. The flat part is normally 100, and rises to 200 on a weapon that has innate blood loss and upgrades with Somber Smithing Stones. The percentage part is 15% against ordinary enemies and other players, and 10.5% against bosses and their companions. Mohg, Lord of Blood is the pointed exception at 7.5%, because the Lord of Blood is not going to be killed by his own trick.

Ten and a half percent does not sound like much until you notice what it ignores. It does not care about the boss defenses, it does not care that your dagger only does 130 physical, and it does not care about damage negation. A boss with 20,000 health hands you 2,100 damage plus the flat 200 every single time that hidden bar fills, and a fast weapon fills it several times per fight. That is why the Assassin builds Dexterity for swing speed and Arcane for buildup instead of chasing a big attack-power number. **Arcane** is the stat that makes the hidden bar fill faster: it raises the potency of blood loss, poison, madness and sleep on any weapon that scales with Arcane, and it also directly raises attack power on weapons carrying the Blood, Poison or Occult affinity. On top of that, each point of Arcane adds 1 to your item discovery, so this build quietly farms better than any other.

The affinity choice is where new players lose the plot, so here it is plainly. An **affinity** is a stamped-on damage profile you apply at a blacksmith with an Ash of War, and you can only stamp the exotic ones once you have found the matching whetblade. The **Black Whetblade** is the one that matters here: it unlocks Poison, Blood and Occult. Blood affinity adds raw blood loss buildup and some Arcane scaling to a weapon that had none, which is how you turn an ordinary sword into a bleed weapon. Occult affinity instead takes a weapon that already bleeds on its own and converts its scaling into Arcane, so that both your damage and your buildup grow off one stat. The rule of thumb: if the weapon has no innate bleed, stamp Blood on it; if it already bleeds by itself, stamp Occult and let Arcane feed both halves. Weapons that upgrade with Somber Smithing Stones - Reduvia, Rivers of Blood, Eleonora's Poleblade - refuse affinities entirely and are already tuned for you, so leave them alone.

The third pillar is the critical attack, and it is the reason this build carries daggers even after it can swing a katana. A **backstab** is a light attack pressed while standing behind a roughly human-sized enemy; a **riposte** is the follow-up after a parry, a broken guard, or a shattered stance meter. Daggers have by a wide margin the best critical multipliers in the game - roughly 294% of your attack power on a backstab and 420% on a riposte, against 220% to 263% for a colossal weapon. The Misericorde pushes that further with a 140 critical rating, an extra 40% on top of an already absurd number, which is why a knife nobody would use for regular swings deletes a knight from behind. Stack the **Dagger Talisman** (critical damage x1.17) with the **Assassin's Crimson Dagger** (10% of your maximum health plus 85 HP back on every critical) and each backstab is both your damage and your healing.

Everything else on the list is glue. **Ash of War: Seppuku** cuts your own health to raise attack power and blood-loss potency, and it is the single largest damage swing available to a bleed build - note it will not go on daggers, throwing blades, backhand blades or colossal swords, so it lives on your katana. **Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step** costs 5 FP and turns you briefly invisible mid-dodge while covering far more ground than a normal roll, which is what lets a 26-Endurance character stand inside a boss combo. **Lord of Blood's Exultation** reads any blood loss within seven metres, including your own from Seppuku, and hands you +20% attack for 20 seconds; the **White Mask** helmet reads the same trigger for another +10%, and a Mimic Tear bleeding its own copy of your katana keeps both lit permanently. The successive-attack talismans stack on top: **Winged Sword Insignia** gives 3%/5%/10% as you keep landing hits, and the **Rotten Winged Sword Insignia** upgrades that curve to 6%/8%/13%. A fast weapon feeds all of it at once, which is the whole thesis - speed is not a style choice here, it is the damage formula.
firstHour: Take the Bandit and pick a Golden Seed as your keepsake, then clear the Cave of Knowledge to learn the light attack and the roll. You already hold the **Great Knife**, whose free Quickstep skill costs 3 FP and does most of what Bloodhound's Step will later do, so there is no early upgrade panic. Ride south past the Church of Elleh, grab Torrent from Melina at any evening grace, and go straight for the riverbed by Murkwater Cave to bait the Nerijus invasion for **Reduvia** - at 13 Dexterity and 13 Arcane it is legal for you on hour one and it bleeds harder than anything else in Limgrave. Then run Deathtouched Catacombs in Stormhill for the **Uchigatana** and the **Assassin's Crimson Dagger**. Buy **Ash of War: Quickstep** from Bernahl at the Warmaster's Shack for 800 runes so your katana has an escape too, and spend your first ten levels on Vigor rather than Dexterity, because the Assassin has no armour worth the name and every plan you have assumes you survive the first mistake.

name: The Giant Crusher
tagline: A boulder on a stick, swung with both hands until the boss falls over.
fantasy: You are the slowest thing on the battlefield and the only thing that matters. Every swing is a commitment, every landed hit folds an enemy's guard, and bosses that shrug off a hundred sword pokes get flattened in three. You do not dodge much because you do not have to - you eat the hit, finish the wind-up, and watch the health bar fall off a cliff.

route.text: Beat Soldier of Godrick - the tutorial arena at the bottom of the Cave of Knowledge, straight down from the Stranded Graveyard.
Get Whetstone Knife - cellar chest in the Gatefront Ruins, up the road from the First Step grace. This is the key that lets you change Ashes of War at any site of grace.

Get Greataxe and Axe Talisman - the axe rides in a troll-drawn carriage on the road west of the Waypoint Ruins (drop a troll, then open the chest); the talisman is in a chest in the Mistwood Ruins cellar in eastern Limgrave, with a runebear roaming near the way in.

Get Greenspill Crystal Tear and Strength-knot Crystal Tear - the first sits on an altar beside the Mistwood minor Erdtree, the second in a stone bowl on the cliff north-east of the Stormhill Shack under a troll's nose. Mixed into the Physick they give +15 percent max stamina for 180 seconds and +10 Strength for 3 minutes, the latter reading as +15 while two-handing.

Get Ash of War: Endure and Ash of War: Golden Vow - buy Endure from Knight Bernahl at the Warmaster's Shack for 600 runes, then hunt the mounted Godrick Knight on the hill north-east of the shack for Golden Vow.

Buy Zweihander - the Isolated Merchant's Shack at the western tip of the peninsula sells it for 3,500 runes, and 13 Strength two-handed makes it the cheapest genuine colossal sword you can hold this early.

Get Grafted Blade Greatsword - fight down through Castle Morne to the arena above the sea. Its Oath of Vengeance skill raises every attribute by 5 for a full minute, which is a fat early-game damage buff on top of the weapon itself.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gate arena on the ramp up to Stormveil Castle. Two-hand, walk sideways under his sweeps, and punish the long recoveries rather than trading.

Get Claw Talisman, then beat Godrick the Grafted - the talisman is on a corpse reached by climbing the sandbags and roofs south of the Rampart Tower grace inside Stormveil. Leave the castle at roughly level 40.

Get Ash of War: Braggart's Roar - kill the teardrop scarab that runs the Ravine-Veiled Village in northern Liurnia, just north of its grace. It raises attack, defence and stamina recovery at once, so it is the buff you use when you cannot afford a second weapon slot.

Get Starscourge Heirloom and Ash of War: Lion's Claw - the talisman (+5 Strength) is in a chest under the canopy on the upper platform of Fort Gael in western Caelid; the ash drops from the Elder Lion penned on the fort's dirt floor, which cannot leave that floor, so a bow trivialises it.
Get Ruins Greatsword - the duo in the Redmane Castle plaza. They vanish while the Radahn Festival is running, so clear them before you set the festival in motion.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the Wailing Dunes, once the festival is on. Summon every NPC sign, keep Torrent under you, and let the colossal do the closing work between his volleys. Around level 80.
Get Mimic Tear Ashes - Radahn's death drops a star that tears Nokron open; the ash waits in a chest behind a Stonesword Key imp statue. It copies your gear exactly, so it hits as hard as you do.

Get Bull-Goat's Talisman, Opaline Hardtear and Stonebarb Cracked Tear - the talisman is on a corpse left of the runebear chamber in Dragonbarrow Cave beneath the minor Erdtree in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow; the two tears drop together from the Putrid Avatar at the minor Erdtree north of Fort Faroth. Stonebarb is the one that matters here: +30 percent poise, stance and stamina damage for 30 seconds.

Get Great-Jar's Arsenal - speak to the Great Jar out in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow and beat all three Knights of the Great Jar it summons. Nineteen percent more equip load is what makes the heavy armor plan legal.

Get Giant-Crusher and Troll's Golden Sword - the Giant-Crusher is chested in a carriage south of the Outer Wall Phantom Tree grace; the golden sword sits in a carriage inside the Leyndell soldier camp between the Erdtree-Gazing Hill and Altus Highway Junction graces. At 26.5 weight it is among the heaviest armaments in the game, and it is this build's endgame weapon.
Get Great Club - Old Altus Tunnel, which costs two Stonesword Keys to open. It asks only 24 Strength two-handed, well under what the Giant-Crusher demands, so it bridges the gap while you level.

Get Ash of War: Royal Knight's Resolve, Ritual Sword Talisman and Leaden Hardtear - the ash is on a corpse in a sealed room off the Volcano Manor shortcut (two Stonesword Keys, then a walk across hanging cages); the talisman is chested in the Lux Ruins cellar behind a demi-human queen; the tear drops from the Ulcerated Tree Spirit at the minor Erdtree east of the Road of Iniquity.

Get Prelate's Inferno Crozier and Fire Scorpion Charm - the Fire Prelate stomping around Fort Laiedd west of Volcano Manor drops the crozier once per playthrough, and the charm hangs on a wooden catwalk on the outside of the fort's rampart.

Get Bull-Goat Armor and its helm, gauntlets and greaves - join Volcano Manor, kill Old Knight Istvan for Tanith, take the letter from Patches, and put down Great Horned Tragoth when he invades you in Liurnia. At 63 total weight it is the heaviest set in the game and ties for the best poise.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the throne arena at the top of the capital. His combos are long, so bank your swings for the pauses rather than forcing them.
Beat Fire Giant - Flame Peak, at the end of the Forbidden Lands road. Hit the shackled leg until he topples, then work the eye. Level 125 by this point.

Get Shard of Alexander, then beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - Iron Fist Alexander asks for a last duel out in the ruins; win it and he hands over the shard, worth 15 percent more damage on every skill you own.

Get Erdtree's Favor +2 - once the capital has turned to ash, head west from the Grand Lift of Rold, down the stairs, and south through the cinders to a corpse hanging off a raised tree root. Three Ulcerated Tree Spirits patrol that field, so hug the walls.

Get Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman - from the Drainage Channel grace in Elphael, cross the roots east to a church roof, drop through the hole and follow the rafters south-west to a chest. Twenty percent physical negation is the largest single defensive item in the game.
Beat Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing and Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Hoarah Loux) - both wait on the road up through the ashen capital to the Erdtree.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the arena at the foot of the Erdtree. Level 150 with the Giant-Crusher at maximum reinforcement.

Beat Mohg, Lord of Blood - take the north-western portal in the snowfield to Mohgwyn Palace, win the fight, then touch the withered arm on the cocoon behind his arena to be pulled into the Land of Shadow.

Get Ash of War: Savage Lion's Claw - in a small camp north-west of the Three-Path Cross grace, west of the Run-Down Traveler's Rest. It is the DLC rework of Lion's Claw, adding an optional second strike to the somersault. Spend your first Scadutree Fragments the moment you find them, because that blessing is the DLC's real difficulty slider.
Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight - the moonlit arena at the far end of Castle Ensis, which gates the road up onto the plateau.
Beat Golden Hippopotamus - the courtyard bruiser inside the keep. It is optional and it is also the single best stance-break practice fight in the DLC.

Get Two-Handed Sword Talisman and Verdigris Discus - the talisman is in a chest up the stairs past the Horned Warrior in the highest building of the Temple Town Ruins; the discus sits before a goddess statue in the same ruins. Fifteen percent more damage on two-handed attacks is, for this build, a straight fifteen percent on everything.
Beat Promised Consort Radahn - the Gate of Divinity at the top of Enir-Ilim, once Messmer has fallen and the tower is open.

variants.name: The Ruin Bringer
variants.twist: Nine points of Intelligence buy you a shockwave, so the slowest build in the game gets an answer to things it cannot reach.
variants.notes: The Ruins Greatsword needs 34 Strength two-handed and 16 Intelligence, so take Intelligence from 7 to 16 and pay for it out of Endurance. Its Wave of Destruction skill fires a gravity shockwave along the ground, which clears mobs and pokes at bosses from outside their swing range. It upgrades with Somber Smithing Stones, so it reaches full power on one stone per level instead of the standard weapon's twelve-stone appetite - a real saving if you find it early. Because you are now paying for a skill rather than a somersault, Shard of Alexander goes from nice to mandatory.

route.text: Clear the Redmane Castle plaza for Ruins Greatsword - now the main event rather than a detour, and it must happen before the Radahn Festival begins or the pair will not be standing there.

variants.name: The Prelate
variants.twist: Trade raw physical numbers for fire, and charge through crowds with a burning anvil instead of stopping to swing at them.
variants.notes: Prelate's Charge sprays flame and then runs forward for as long as you hold it, at 7 FP per second, which turns catacomb corridors and camp clears into one button. Fire Scorpion Charm gives 12 percent more fire attack at the cost of taking 10 percent more physical damage, a trade that only makes sense when a real chunk of your damage is fire in the first place. The crozier asks 30 Strength two-handed and 8 Dexterity, so it comes online far earlier than the Giant-Crusher and can carry you from the Altus Plateau to the end. Keep Bull-Goat's Talisman equipped here, because the extra physical damage you are agreeing to eat has to be paid for somewhere.

route.text: Kill the Fire Prelate at Fort Laiedd for Prelate's Inferno Crozier, then lift Fire Scorpion Charm off the rampart catwalk on the way out - one trip arms the whole variant.

variants.name: The Shadow Behemoth
variants.twist: Everything the DLC hands out happens to be aimed at exactly this build, so the Land of Shadow becomes the build's proper endgame rather than a bonus.

swaps.to: Ash of War: Savage Lion's Claw

variants.notes: The Two-Handed Sword Talisman gives 15 percent on two-handed attacks, and you never one-hand anything, so it beats the jump-attack talisman on any swing that is not a jump. The Verdigris Discus rewards exactly the sin this build commits: nothing under 70 percent equip load, 10 percent defence between 70 and 100 percent, and 20 percent once you hit 100 percent, which is the very edge of being overloaded and unable to roll at all. Pair it with the shield-and-guard-counter playstyle so the lost mobility costs you nothing. Push Scadutree Blessing hard: at the maximum level 20, from all 50 fragments, you deal 2.05 times damage and take 0.487 times damage inside the Land of Shadow, which is a bigger swing than any weapon choice in this file.

route.text: Detour to Temple Town Ruins early for Verdigris Discus and Two-Handed Sword Talisman - both are pure passive upgrades, so grabbing them first makes everything after them easier.

pvp: Meta level is 125 for most invasion brackets and 150 for arena, and the stat sheets above land on both on purpose. Drop the **Axe Talisman** the moment you go against players - its charged-attack bonus is bugged to a flat 1x in PvP and does literally nothing. The rest of the kit is halved but still real: **Claw Talisman** falls from 15 to 7.5 percent, **Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman** from 20 to 5 percent, and the DLC **Two-Handed Sword Talisman** from 15 to 10 percent, which makes it the best offensive slot you own in a duel. Your win condition is the hyper-armor trade - let them commit to a light-attack string, swing through it, and take the exchange your poise and their lack of it makes lopsided. Your loss condition is whiffing, so never throw a charged heavy at a moving target and save Lion's Claw for a punish rather than an opener.
why:
The whole build rests on one rule the game never spells out for you: holding a weapon with both hands multiplies your Strength by 1.5, rounded up, and that multiplied number is used for BOTH the weapon's requirement and its damage scaling. So 40 Strength wields anything that asks for 60, and the 54 Strength on the level-125 sheet is read by the game as 81. That is why the stat targets stop climbing Strength around the mid fifties and dump everything else into survival - the extra points would be buying a curve that has already gone nearly flat, while Vigor is still handing you whole extra hits of health.

The second pillar is stance. Every enemy carries a hidden poise meter - roughly 15 to 65 on ordinary foes, 80 to 120 on bosses - that your attacks chip away at separately from their health. Empty it and they drop to a knee, wide open for a riposte, which is the free critical hit that does enormous damage. That meter refills at 13 points a second, but only after a delay equal to the enemy's base poise divided by 13, so a 120-poise boss sits there defenceless-ish for about nine seconds before it starts recovering. Colossal weapons are the fastest way to empty it: the hammer-type colossals deal the highest base stance damage of any armament in the game (7.5, against 6 for the axe-type ones). Two heavy swings and a jump attack is often a full stance break on a boss that would take a dagger user a full minute of chip.

Third: you win trades on purpose. Heavy armor and the **Bull-Goat's Talisman** - which cuts incoming poise damage by 25 percent - push you past the poise numbers that matter, 51 (soak one ordinary enemy attack without flinching) and 101 (soak two of them, or one heavy one). Above those lines you simply do not get interrupted mid-swing, so the slow wind-up that looks like a liability stops being one. The Lion's Claw skill goes further and runs on super armor, which ignores poise maths altogether for the duration of the somersault. That is the button you press when a boss is already committed to its own attack and you want to swap damage with it.

Everything hanging off those pillars is multiplier stacking, and the multipliers here are unusually large because colossal attacks are single huge numbers rather than many small ones. **Claw Talisman** adds 15 percent to jump attacks, which is your bread-and-butter opener. **Axe Talisman** turns charged heavy attacks into 1.1x. **Shard of Alexander** adds 15 percent to skills, which is Lion's Claw and Royal Knight's Resolve. **Ritual Sword Talisman** adds a flat 10 percent while you are at full health, and since you rarely get interrupted you are at full health a lot. The cost of all that iron is weight: equip load under 30 percent rolls light, 30 to 70 percent rolls medium, and 70 percent or more gives you a heavy roll with almost twice the recovery animation. **Great-Jar's Arsenal** (+19 percent load) and **Erdtree's Favor +2** (+4 percent HP, +10 percent stamina, +8 percent load) exist so you can wear the heaviest set in the game and still land under 70 percent.
firstHour: Pick Hero and take the Golden Seed as your keepsake, since one extra flask charge is worth more at level 7 than anything else on that list. Beat the tutorial, come out at the Stranded Graveyard, and ride Torrent north up the road to the Gatefront Ruins, where the cellar chest holds the **Whetstone Knife**. From the very first swing, hold your **Battle Axe** with both hands - 16 Strength becomes 24, and the damage difference is immediately obvious. Ride west on the road past the Waypoint Ruins until you hear a troll-drawn carriage, kill one troll to stop it, and open the chest for the **Greataxe**, which you can two-hand at 20 Strength within a couple of levels. Then go collect the **Strength-knot Crystal Tear** from the cliff bowl north-east of the Stormhill Shack, and spend everything else on Vigor until you are comfortable being hit.

name: The Dragon Priest
tagline: Eat dragon hearts, breathe scarlet rot, and let the boss rot to death.
fantasy: You stop asking the Golden Order for power and start eating it raw. Every dragon you put down becomes a heart on an altar, and every heart becomes a piece of a dragon grafted onto you - a jaw, a claw, a lungful of rot. Fights turn quiet: you land one long breath, back off, and watch the health bar drain on its own.

route.text: Grab Dragon Communion Seal - Fringefolk Hero's Grave, entered by the gate below the Stranded Graveyard that costs two Stonesword Keys; go down two ramps, right at the split, up two more, and kill the spectral Banished Knight in the small room at the end.
Kill Flying Dragon Agheel - he drops into the shallows of Agheel Lake in southern Limgrave, northwest of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins, for 5,000 runes and your first Dragon Heart.

Buy Dragonfire - the Church of Dragon Communion stands on an island off the west coast, reached by fighting through Coastal Cave; the altar takes one Dragon Heart and the spell wants 15 Faith and 12 Arcane.
Pick up Faith-knot Crystal Tear - in a bowl at the cliff edge north of the Demi-Human Forest Ruins, east of the Church of Pilgrimage, among the Miranda Sprouts; it is +10 Faith for three minutes.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gate at the foot of Stormveil Castle, worth 12,000 runes and the Talisman Pouch that gives you a third talisman slot.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the top of Stormveil Castle; his Great Rune is one of the two you will need to open Leyndell, and you should be near level 40 leaving Limgrave.

Take Radagon Icon - Academy of Raya Lucaria: from the Debate Parlor step into the courtyard, go right around the building, hop the fence, climb the ladder and jump through the broken window to the chest.

Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the Grand Library at the top of the academy; she survives the fight and will rebuild your stats afterwards for one Larval Tear, which is your safety net if this spread does not suit you.

Kill Elder Dragon Greyoll - the sleeping mountain of a dragon south of Fort Faroth on Greyoll's Dragonbarrow; she never moves, the six lesser dragons around her share her health bar, and she pays 74,290 runes and five Dragon Hearts at once.

Take Radagon's Soreseal - inside Fort Faroth: up the ladder at the entrance, across the roof and down into the rat-filled barn. It is +5 Vigor, Endurance, Strength and Dexterity for 15% more damage taken.
Buy Rotten Breath - the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in southern Caelid, one Dragon Heart. This is the spell the entire build is arranged around; put it in your first memory slot and leave it there.
Kill Decaying Ekzykes - he stalks the rotted flats northwest of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion for 38,000 runes and a heart, and killing him puts Ekzykes's Decay on the altar for two more.
Buy Greyoll's Roar - the same altar, three Dragon Hearts, and it only appears in the list once Greyoll is dead. It costs two memory slots and strips attack power and defence off everything near you.
Buy Dragonclaw - one Dragon Heart at the cathedral; 17 Faith and 13 Arcane buys you two enormous claw slams with shockwaves, which is the closest thing this build has to a melee weapon.
Take Faithful's Canvas Talisman - Sellia Crystal Tunnel, on a corpse off the right-hand side of the main path with two Pests standing over it.

Earn Clawmark Seal - hand your first Deathroot to Gurranq at the Bestial Sanctum on the northern tip of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow; show a Deathroot to D, Hunter of the Dead first and the sending gate that takes you there appears on your map.

Take Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear - from the Putrid Avatar at the Minor Erdtree down the cliffs northeast of the Smoldering Church; it is +20% fire damage for three minutes, which is Dragonfire's payday. You want roughly level 80 by the time Caelid is behind you.

Take Mimic Tear Ashes - a chest behind an imp statue seal. It copies your entire loadout including the seals and casts your dragon spells alongside you for 660 HP rather than FP, and the Mimic Tear boss in the same city drops the Silver Tear Mask, which is +8 Arcane for a 5% cut to physical attack power.
Take Kindred of Rot's Exultation - from the pair of Kindred of Rot in Seethewater Cave in the middle of Mt. Gelmir.
Learn Golden Vow - on a body in the Corpse-Stench Shack, east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity; Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater invades at the same spot, so clear her first.

Take Erdtree Seal - Volcano Manor, in an open cell just northwest of the Prison Town Church grace with an Omenkiller stalking the corridor. Hold it until 40 Faith, where it starts to out-scale everything else in a Faith-only slot.
Take Gravel Stone Seal - from the spear-carrying Leyndell Knight standing to the left of the front gate of the Fortified Manor.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the Elden Throne, 120,000 runes and his Great Rune. You should be around level 125 here.
Take Mushroom Crown - on a corpse on top of a pillar in the ruins in the southeast of the lake; ride the raised platforms and do not linger in the water.
Beat Fire Giant - Flame Peak. Rot lands on him easily and his wounded right ankle takes double damage in the first phase, so plant a breath and go for the ankle while it ticks.

Buy Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear - the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook lies on the floor of the giant hall between the Crumbling Beast Grave Depths and Tempest-Facing Balcony graces; give it to Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows and the spell costs 8,500 runes.
Beat Dragonlord Placidusax - an optional Legend-tier fight worth 280,000 runes whose Remembrance of the Dragonlord trades with Finger Reader Enia for Placidusax's Ruin.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - 220,000 runes, and unbinding the Rune of Death burns the thorns off the Erdtree.
Beat Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Hoarah Loux) - the Elden Throne again, now the Ashen Capital, for 300,000 runes.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - inside the Erdtree, 500,000 runes for the pair. Level 150 is a comfortable finishing number.

Buy Ghostflame Breath - take the Pillar Path highroad south from Castle Ensis, go through the Dragon's Pit, and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion sits about a kilometer south of the Foot of the Jagged Peak; three Dragon Hearts for a frostbite breath at 23 Faith and 15 Arcane.
Kill Ancient Dragon Senessax - partway up the storm-struck slope, among the dragon corpses.
Beat Bayle the Dread - the summit; he weighs in at 490,000 runes, is weak to piercing damage, and Drake Warrior Igon can be summoned if you have found his Furled Finger.
Take Bayle's Tyranny - offer the Heart of Bayle back at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion. It asks 49 Arcane and no Faith whatsoever, which is the purest expression of this build in the game.

variants.name: The Dragon Cult Lightning Priest
variants.twist: Trade most of the Arcane for Faith and throw red lightning off the Gravel Stone Seal instead of breathing rot.
variants.notes: Push Faith to 60 and let Arcane sit near its base; the Gravel Stone Seal's 15% single-wield boost to Dragon Cult incantations applies to every red lightning spell, and holding a second seal in the off-hand raises that to 32.25%. You give up the free damage-over-time and the Kindred of Rot's Exultation trigger, and you get a fast, spammable ranged spell that works on the rot-resistant bosses where the breath line stalls. Erdtree Seal becomes your best pure-Faith option once you pass 40 Faith. Keep one breath memorized anyway for crowds.

route.text: Skip Dragon Communion Seal and run the Finger Seal until Leyndell - the Fringefolk Hero's Grave detour costs two Stonesword Keys you do not need for this line.
Take Gravel Stone Seal early - the spear-carrying Leyndell Knight by the Fortified Manor gate is reachable the moment you enter the capital, and this seal is the whole variant.

variants.name: The Rot Bomber
variants.twist: Dump everything into Arcane, keep Faith at the bare minimum to cast the breaths, and win by stacking rot procs and the damage bonuses they switch on.
variants.notes: Faith stops at 24, which is exactly what Dragonmaw asks for and one point past Ekzykes's Decay, and every remaining point goes to Arcane, which is the only stat the Dragon Communion Seal scales at C. Wear Mushroom Crown alongside Kindred of Rot's Exultation so a single proc turns on +20% and +10% at once, then follow with Dragonmaw at 24 Faith and 16 Arcane while both timers run. It is a glass build - 9.1 units of mushroom on your head is not armor - so keep Vigor climbing and treat the Mimic Tear as your aggro sponge.

variants.name: Bayle's Heir
variants.twist: A Shadow of the Erdtree finish that leans on the pure-Arcane dragon spells and the DLC's own power curve instead of character level.
variants.notes: Bayle's Tyranny costs 46 FP and two memory slots and requires 49 Arcane with zero Faith, so an Arcane-heavy Dragon Priest walks into it while a Faith build cannot. Note that the Heart of Bayle cannot be duplicated, so Bayle's Tyranny and Bayle's Flame Lightning are mutually exclusive in a single playthrough. In the Land of Shadow your Scadutree Blessing matters far more than your rune level - there are 50 Scadutree Fragments, the blessing caps at level 20, and a maxed blessing is worth roughly a 200% damage increase and a 51% cut to damage taken inside the DLC only. Collect fragments before you level.

pvp:
At the 125 and 150 metas this is a zoning build, not a dueling one. Every dragon breath has a long,
loud wind-up and a fixed direction, so treat Rotten Breath as area denial - spray the ground someone
has to cross rather than aiming at their body - and let the rot buildup force the trade. Radagon
Icon's +30 virtual Dexterity is close to mandatory here because the raw cast times are punishing.
Rot still builds on players, but most duels end long before the tick decides anything, so use it to
herd an opponent off the ground they want rather than as your win condition. Avoid Dragonmaw and Greyoll's Roar entirely against a
human opponent - the commitment is enormous - and remember that Golden Vow is halved in PvP (7.5%
attack, 5% negation) so buffing mid-fight is rarely worth the opening you give away.
why:
Almost every incantation in the game asks only for Faith. Dragon Communion incantations are the
exception: they charge you in Faith *and* Arcane, and they pay you back through a seal nobody else
wants. The Dragon Communion Seal needs only 10 Faith and 10 Arcane to hold, weighs nothing, upgrades
on Somber Smithing Stones, and at +10 it carries D scaling in Faith and C scaling in Arcane for 106
incantation scaling. "Incantation scaling" is the single number a seal feeds into a spell's damage,
the way a sword's attack rating feeds into a swing - raise the number, every spell you cast off that
seal hits harder. Arcane is a stat most builds treat as a bleed-and-item-discovery dump. Here it is
your main damage stat, and the seal is the only thing in the game that pays you properly for it.

What you buy with those stats is scarlet rot. Rotten Breath costs 36 FP, wants 15 Faith and 12
Arcane, and can hit a target up to three times in one breath; Ekzykes's Decay is the bigger version
at 23 Faith and 15 Arcane. Rot is a *buildup* status: each hit adds to an invisible meter on the
target, and when the meter fills the status "procs" and starts draining their health over time,
independent of anything else you do. That is the whole trick. A breath that deals mediocre direct
damage is fine, because the rot it plants keeps working while you sprint away, heal, and re-buff.
Resistance to rot is governed by Immunity, which climbs as you level Vigor - so the same breath that
melts a soft enemy will need two or three applications on a heavy one. It is worth knowing the
spread before you commit: the Fire Giant's scarlet rot threshold starts at 566, while Starscourge
Radahn is a deliberate wall at 1,295 despite being the poster child for rot in the story. Plan to
out-damage a few bosses the old-fashioned way rather than assuming rot solves everything.

The talismans are where the build turns from "fun" into "fast". Flock's Canvas Talisman adds 8% to
incantation attack power and Faithful's Canvas Talisman adds 4%, and the two stack multiplicatively
rather than cancelling. Kindred of Rot's Exultation is the real prize: it grants +20% damage for 20
seconds whenever anyone within 7 meters is suffering poison or scarlet rot - and your own rotted
target counts. Mushroom Crown does the same thing for +10% if you can carry 9.1 units of headgear.
So the loop is: breathe once to plant rot, the rot procs, your own damage jumps by a fifth, and every
follow-up lands harder. Ritual Sword Talisman adds another 10% while you are at full health, and
Radagon Icon is worth a slot purely because it grants +30 virtual Dexterity, which shortens cast
animations - and dragon breaths are among the longest animations in the game.

Two traps to avoid. Shard of Alexander boosts *skills* (the special attacks bound to weapons and
Ashes of War) by 15% and does nothing at all for incantations, so it is a wasted slot here no matter
how many build videos wear it. And Placidusax's Ruin, the 80 FP, three-slot showpiece you get from
the Dragonlord's remembrance, belongs to no incantation school, which means no sacred seal boosts it
- it also asks 36 Faith and zero Arcane, so it is a spectacle spell rather than a core one. The
seals you actually stack are the Dragon Communion Seal for the breath line and the Gravel Stone Seal
for the Dragon Cult lightning: the Gravel Stone gives 15% to Dragon Cult incantations when
single-wielded and 32.25% with one in each hand, and its boost applies to Dragon Cult spells cast off
the *other* seal as long as a Gravel Stone is in your off-hand. That off-hand quirk is how a
late-game Dragon Priest runs rot and red lightning out of the same loadout.
firstHour:
Pick the Prophet: it starts at level 7 with 16 Faith and 10 Arcane, which is exactly the doorway the
Dragon Communion Seal asks for, and take the Golden Seed as your keepsake so you get an extra flask
charge immediately. Walk through the Cave of Knowledge for the tutorial, then head out into Limgrave
and ignore the Tree Sentinel on the road. Get two Stonesword Keys and open Fringefolk Hero's Grave
below the Stranded Graveyard for the Dragon Communion Seal - the grave is nasty at level 10, but you
only need to reach the Banished Knight, not clear it, and Erdtree's Favor is on an altar deeper in
for +3% HP, +7% stamina and +5% equip load. Then ride to Agheel Lake, learn the dragon's fire-breath
timings from horseback, and kill him for your first Dragon Heart. Spend it on Dragonfire at the
Church of Dragon Communion out past Coastal Cave, put a few levels into Vigor and Faith, and you are
already the thing this guide is about.

name: The Prophet
tagline: Lightning, holy fire and healing from a seal - fights won at arm's length
fantasy: You hold a seal instead of a sword, and the sky answers. Bolts fall on things that were about to reach you, wounds close between casts, and the gold-and-white light you throw is the same light the Erdtree runs on. It is the calmest way to play Elden Ring, right up until you drop a charged dragon-cult spear on something and it simply stops existing.

route.text: Begin as the Prophet, who wakes up already holding a Finger Seal, a Short Spear, Catch Flame and Heal - no other origin starts this ready to cast.

Get Ash of War: Sacred Blade from the scarab on the hill past the pond northwest of the Third Church of Marika, and Ash of War: Golden Vow from the mounted Godrick Knight on the hill northeast of Warmaster's Shack in Stormhill. Take the Whetstone Knife out of the Gatefront Ruins cellar chest first or you cannot apply either.

Get Erdtree's Favor - deep inside the Fringefolk Hero's Grave below the Stranded Graveyard. It costs two Stonesword Keys and a nervous run past a chariot that cannot be killed, and the HP, stamina and equip load it hands back never stop earning the slot.

Get Faith-knot Crystal Tear - in a hollow of ground north of the Demi-Human Forest Ruins near the cliff edge, just east of the Church of Pilgrimage, with Miranda Sprouts watching over it. Three minutes of +10 Faith is a whole extra seal's worth of scaling for one boss attempt.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - at the gate of Stormveil Castle. Open with the Sacred Blade wave from outside his reach and trade only once his combo has visibly ended.

Get Godslayer's Seal - in the chest behind the Stonesword Key fog in the Stormveil Castle cellar, entered on the left of the courtyard past a knot of rats. The Godskin Prayerbook sits behind the same fog; take both.
Beat Godrick the Grafted, found at the top of Stormveil Castle in its throne room. You want to be around level 40 here, holding 25 Faith and 25 Vigor.

Get Two Fingers Heirloom - in the cellar of the Purified Ruins in the south of the region. The stairs down are boarded over; you break the planks by rolling into them. Five free Faith is five levels you never have to buy.

Take the Dragon Cult Prayerbook from the Leyndell Knight south of the Artist's Shack to Miriel, Pastor of Vows at the Church of Vows, and buy Lightning Spear for 6,000 runes and Honed Bolt for 7,000. This is the moment the build stops being a starter kit.

Get Radagon Icon and beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the talisman is in a chest on an upper landing of the Raya Lucaria Academy, reached from the Debate Parlour grace by going out into the courtyard, round the building, over a fence, up a ladder and in through a broken window; Rennala waits in the Grand Library above, and beating her unlocks respeccing, so from here every stat mistake is refundable.
Get Flame, Grant Me Strength - on a corpse on the eastern side of Fort Gael, watched over by two flame-throwing chariots.
Get Faithful's Canvas Talisman - on a body off the right-hand side of the main path through the Sellia Crystal Tunnel, with two pests hovering beside it.
Get Sacred Scorpion Charm - kill Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater when she invades you near the Smoldering Church in the northwest of the region.

Beat Starscourge Radahn - the festival arena in the Wailing Dunes east of Redmane Castle. Torrent is allowed in the arena, so ride the perimeter, throw Lightning Spear between his charges and call in every summon sign scattered around the field.

Get Mimic Tear Ashes - in a chest behind a Stonesword Key imp statue, reachable only through the crater Radahn's falling star tore open near Fort Haight. The mimic copies your gear and casts your spells, and it is the single biggest quality-of-life pickup on this route.
Get Golden Vow - inside the Corpse-Stench Shack east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity.

Get Cerulean Hidden Tear - dropped by the Ulcerated Tree Spirit (Mt. Gelmir) coiled round the Minor Erdtree south of the Road of Iniquity grace. Ten seconds of free casting turns one flask sip into an artillery barrage.

Get Erdtree Seal - in an open cell northwest of the Prison Town Church grace inside Volcano Manor, with an Omenkiller loitering nearby. It demands 40 Faith to hold, which is exactly your level 80 target.
Get Godfrey Icon - beat Godefroy the Grafted in the Golden Lineage Evergaol in the south of the plateau.

Get Gravel Stone Seal and Blessing of the Erdtree - the seal drops from the spear-carrying Leyndell Knight standing to the left of the front gate of the Fortified Manor, and the incantation lies near the Queen's Bedchamber grace. Take the incantation BEFORE you fight Maliketh: the capital turns to ash afterwards and this pickup is gone for the rest of the playthrough.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the Erdtree Sanctuary at the summit of the capital.
Get Frozen Lightning Spear - a guaranteed drop from the Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella in the river depths. It costs 34 Faith and staggers almost anything that is not itself a dragon.

Get Elden Stars - at the far end of the ant-choked cave immediately west of the Great Waterfall Crest grace, up one of the enormous roots. Fifty Faith buys a slow drifting swarm of holy motes that is unfair in the best possible way.

Beat Fire Giant - the Forge of the Giants. Buff with Golden Vow and Flame, Grant Me Strength before the fog and re-apply both between phases; the fight is long enough that an 80-second buff will lapse.

Take the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook from the floor of the great hall between the Crumbling Beast Grave Depths and Tempest-Facing Balcony graces back to Miriel and buy Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear, then grab Golden Lightning Fortification from the scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift grace. Sixty percent less lightning damage for seventy seconds makes the rest of this ruin trivial.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - the Dragon Temple Rooftop.

Get Erdtree Heal and Erdtree's Favor +2 - the Ashen Capital versions of two earlier pickups. The incantation is by the Queen's Bedchamber grace and the talisman hangs from a tree root in the ash to the south, past three Ulcerated Tree Spirits you can hug the walls to avoid.

Beat Mohg, Lord of Blood - the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum in the east of the underground. Send the Mimic Tear in first and expect the second phase to outpace your healing if you are standing anywhere near him.

Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the end of the base game. Save the Cerulean Hidden Tear for the second phase, where ten seconds of free casting lets you empty every spell you have while the beast is drifting.

Enter the Land of Shadow - with Radahn and Mohg both dead, touch the withered arm in the Cocoon of the Empyrean in Mohg's arena. Then collect Scadutree Fragments obsessively and burn them at any grace: 50 exist in the expansion, Blessing level 20 is the ceiling, and at maximum your damage output roughly doubles while incoming damage is roughly halved. Nothing you levelled matters as much as this.

Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight - inside Castle Ensis, which walls off the road onwards. She is the first genuine skill check of the expansion and a good gauge of whether your Blessing level is high enough.

Get Multilayered Ring of Light - from the phantom Misbegotten Warrior on the main path past the Fissure Waypoint grace. Thirty-six Faith, holy damage, and a hit count that shreds anything that cannot back out of it.

Get Dryleaf Seal - on a cliff facing the water north of the Recluses' River Downstream grace. It lifts ring-of-light incantations by 15%, making it the off-hand seal for a holy loadout the way Gravel Stone is for a lightning one.

Get Fire Knight's Seal and beat Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent) - the seal sits behind the beheaded Marika statue in the largest church of the Church District once the water is drained, guarded by Wego, Fire Knight Elder. Messmer waits deeper in the keep, and his Kindling is what lets you burn the Sealing Tree.
Beat Promised Consort Radahn - the last fight in the Land of Shadow. Golden Lightning Fortification is not optional here, and neither is a high Scadutree Blessing.

variants.name: The Dragon Cult Duelist
variants.twist: Abandon holy damage entirely and run pure lightning, with the boost seal permanently in your off hand so every bolt carries an extra 15% before a talisman touches it.
variants.notes: Sacred Scorpion Charm lifts only holy damage, so on a lightning loadout it contributes nothing while its 10% physical penalty is pure loss - Flock's Canvas Talisman and its flat 8% to all incantations replaces it cleanly. Surrendering a melee weapon for a second seal is the real cost, so this wants Mimic Tear Ashes out on every fight to hold attention while you cast. Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike comes from the same Ancient Dragon Prayerbook as the spear, so it is a free addition once you have made the trip to Farum Azula. Specialising has a price: lightning is one of the most commonly resisted damage types late in the game, so keep Honed Bolt memorised for the fights that shrug off the big spears.

variants.name: The Golden Order Fundamentalist
variants.twist: Split your casting stat between Intelligence and Faith to wield the Golden Order Seal, trading thrown lightning for expanding rings of holy light.
variants.notes: The Golden Order Seal rests at the tree inside the Minor Erdtree Church in the Capital Outskirts, southwest of Leyndell, and asks for 17 Intelligence alongside 17 Faith - move ten points out of Vigor into Intelligence at the level 125 checkpoint and respec at Rennala rather than carrying both stats from the start. It scales D with each of the two, which is worse raw scaling than the Erdtree Seal, so the variant earns it back through the seal's 10% Golden Order boost and by pairing it with the Dryleaf Seal, whose 15% ring bonus stacks on top for Discus of Light, Radagon's Rings of Light and Triple Rings of Light. At three FP a cast, Discus of Light effectively becomes your basic attack. One trap: Elden Stars is an Erdtree incantation rather than a Golden Order one, so the Golden Order Seal does nothing for it.

variants.name: The Black Flame Apostle
variants.twist: Keep the seal you found in Stormveil and build around black flame, whose burn takes a percentage of the target's maximum health rather than a flat number, so it hurts a bloated endgame boss exactly as much as it hurts a rat.
variants.notes: The Godskin Prayerbook you took from the Stormveil cellar unlocks both spells at Miriel or Brother Corhyn for 7,500 runes each. Black Flame asks 20 Faith and 18 FP, and its lingering burn deals 2% of the target's maximum HP plus 20 over two seconds on top of the impact damage. Godslayer's Seal raises godslayer incantations by 10%, or 21% with one in each hand, though that boost pointedly skips Black Flame Blade. Because Godslayer's Seal is the strongest pure-Faith seal from 27 Faith all the way to 68, this is the hardest-hitting of the three variants below level 125 and the one that falls behind afterwards - move back to the Erdtree Seal once you cross into the seventies.

pvp: The standard invasion brackets are 125 and 150; at 125 this build runs 60 Faith and 60 Vigor, and at 150 it pushes Faith to the 80 hard cap. Understand before you queue that most of the numbers above are roughly halved against players: Golden Vow gives 7.5% attack instead of 15%, Golden Lightning Fortification cuts lightning by 20% rather than 60%, and Sacred Scorpion Charm's holy bonus falls to 8% while its physical penalty climbs to 15%. Godfrey Icon carries a documented bug where its charged-spell multiplier does nothing whatsoever for holy damage in PvP, so on a holy loadout that slot is dead weight. Slow telegraphed casts like Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear get rolled through by anyone competent, so your real duelling kit is the fast and cheap end of the list - Discus of Light, Lightning Spear, Catch Flame at kissing range - with Radagon Icon worn permanently, because 30 virtual Dexterity of cast speed is worth more against a human than any damage talisman.
why:
Faith is one of eight attributes, and it is the one that powers incantations - the prayer half of Elden Ring's magic. To cast anything you need two things equipped: a **sacred seal** (a catalyst, held like a weapon) and the incantation itself, which you memorise at a site of grace. Damage does not come from the spell alone. Each seal carries a hidden number the game calls Incantation Scaling, it climbs as your Faith climbs, and every spell you cast is multiplied by it. That single number is why "which seal am I holding" matters more than almost any other choice this build makes.

The seals are a ladder, and the rungs are Faith breakpoints. A **Finger Seal** costs 800 runes from the Twin Maiden Husks and is genuinely the best pure-Faith option below 27 Faith - and it stays ahead of the Erdtree Seal all the way to 66 Faith. The **Godslayer's Seal** takes over from 27 Faith to 68. Only past 68 does the **Erdtree Seal** become the strongest Faith-only catalyst in the game; fully upgraded it reaches 353 Incantation Scaling at 80 Faith while the rest of the field sits between roughly 310 and 330. There is a catch worth planning around: the Erdtree Seal upgrades with Somber Smithing Stones, nine rungs to +10, while the Finger Seal and Godslayer's Seal eat regular Smithing Stones, twenty-five rungs to +25. Somber stones are far easier to come by early, which is why the recommended path is to ride the Finger Seal hard, pick the Godslayer's Seal up in passing at Stormveil, and switch to the Erdtree Seal the moment you reach 40 Faith and can actually hold it.

Boost seals are the trick most new casters miss. A seal that "enhances" a school of incantations applies that bonus even when a different seal does the casting, so long as the boost seal is held in your other hand. The endgame loadout is therefore two seals and no weapon: **Erdtree Seal** in the right hand doing the scaling, **Gravel Stone Seal** in the left contributing its flat 15% to every Dragon Cult incantation, which is what all your lightning is. Hold two Gravel Stone Seals and that bonus compounds to 32.25%, but you then surrender the Erdtree Seal's superior scaling, so one of each is the sane split until very high Faith.

Everything else stacks multipliers on top of that. Faith has soft caps at 18 and 60 and stops paying out entirely at 80, so the tables above land on 60 at level 125 and 80 at level 150 rather than dribbling points past the wall. **Flock's Canvas Talisman** adds 8% to incantation attack power and **Faithful's Canvas Talisman** adds 4%. **Godfrey Icon** adds 15%, but only to spells you actually hold the button to charge, which is how lightning spears want to be thrown anyway. **Sacred Scorpion Charm** buys 12% more holy damage for 10% more physical damage taken, a trade a ranged caster can usually afford. **Radagon Icon** is the quiet star: it grants 30 points of "virtual" Dexterity purely for the purpose of cast animations, so your spells come out visibly faster without costing a single level. Buffs go on before the fight starts - **Golden Vow** for 80 seconds of +15% attack and 10% less damage taken, **Flame, Grant Me Strength** for 30 seconds of +20% physical and fire attack - and Mind is what pays for all of it, which is why it climbs steadily rather than sitting at the class base.
firstHour: Pick Prophet, take whichever keepsake appeals, and walk out of the Stranded Graveyard already able to cast: Catch Flame for anything that closes the gap, Heal for everything else. Do not fight the golden knight on horseback outside the Church of Elleh - ride past him and keep your runes. Put your first handful of levels into Mind so you can cast twice in a row, then loot the Gatefront Ruins cellar chest for the Whetstone Knife and go collect the Sacred Blade ash northwest of the Third Church of Marika; on the Short Spear it gives you a ranged option that costs FP you can spare and a melee option that is not embarrassing. Light graces until Melina offers you the Roundtable Hold, where Brother Corhyn sells Flame Sling for 800 runes, and pick up the Cipher Pata by dropping over the balcony rail there into the rooms on the left. By the time you knock on Stormveil's gate you want 20 to 25 Faith, roughly 20 Vigor, and the habit of opening every fight from as far away as the room allows.
