name: The Frost Knight
tagline: Freeze everything, then hit it while its defences are 20% weaker.
fantasy: You fight in a cold blue light. Every swing, every stomp and every spell packs frost into the enemy until the meter fills and the world turns white, and for the next half a minute they take extra damage from absolutely everything you own. By the end you are swinging Ranni's own moonlight greatsword and dropping a dark moon on anything that will not stand still.

route.text: Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - he guards the gate of Stormveil Castle at the top of Stormhill. If he is too much at first, ride past and come back with more Vigor; nothing here is on a timer.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the throne room at the far end of Stormveil Castle.
Get Icerind Hatchet - inside a chest in a small broken tower in southern Temple Quarter, south-west of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. This is your damage for the next twenty levels.
Get Ash of War: Hoarfrost Stomp - an invisible Teardrop Scarab carries it, in the pond south-east of Caria Manor sitting above the ravine. It grants Cold affinity.
Get Frozen Armament - another Scarab drops it, on the road north-west of the Behind Caria Manor grace. 15 Intelligence, 20 FP, and it puts 63 frostbite on your right-hand weapon for sixty seconds.
Get Ash of War: Chilling Mist - from the Scarab in the ruins south-east of Renna's Rise, behind Caria Manor. Same Cold affinity, but a forward slash that leaves your blade frosted for a while.
Get Carian Filigreed Crest - 5,000 runes from Smithing Master Iji, once you have either spoken to Ranni at the top of Ranni's Rise or told him Blaidd sent you.
Get Glintstone Icecrag - 7,500 runes from Preceptor Seluvis. If he is already dead, his bell bearing sells it at the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price.
Beat Royal Revenant - in the Kingsrealm Ruins; the chest behind it holds Frozen Needle, a 2.5 weight thrusting sword with 60 frostbite that wants 18 Dexterity.

Get Graven-School Talisman - Academy of Raya Lucaria. In the room west of the Debate Parlor there is an illusory wall on the north side by an empty bookshelf; hit it, climb the ladder, then drop through the hole past the painting.

Get Radagon Icon - also in the Academy. From the Debate Parlor go out to the courtyard, work around the outside of the building, hop a fence, climb the ladder and enter through the broken window; the chest is on the landing.
Beat Red Wolf of Radagon - the Debate Parlor arena.

Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the Raya Lucaria Grand Library. Her remembrance buys the Carian Regal Scepter from Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold; it needs 60 Intelligence but adds 10% to moon sorceries, which is your late-game staff.

Beat Royal Knight Loretta - the apparition at the Royal Moongazing Grounds inside Caria Manor. She drops the Loretta's Greatbow sorcery, a 26 Intelligence chargeable magic arrow that is your safest long-range poke.

Get Magic Scorpion Charm - give Preceptor Seluvis the Amber Starlight to advance his quest. Do this NOW: handing Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade later ends Seluvis's questline on the spot and the charm is gone for the run.

Beat Erdtree Avatar (Liurnia Northeast) - at the north-eastern Minor Erdtree. It drops the Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear, which is +20% magic damage for 180 seconds in your physick. You should be about level 40 leaving Liurnia.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the festival at Redmane Castle. This is mandatory for the rest of the build, because his death is what drops the stars and opens Nokron.
Get Mimic Tear Ashes - a chest behind an imp statue, so bring a Stonesword Key. A copy of you means a second source of frostbite, which halves the time to every proc.
Get Snow Witch Hat - the chest inside Renna's Rise, which only opens once Ranni's questline has moved past the Fingerslayer Blade handover.

Reach Ainsel River Main - take the waygate in Renna's Rise, grab the miniature Ranni near where you land, and speak to her three times. The Baleful Shadow that invades past Nokstella's waterfall basin drops the Discarded Palace Key, which opens the chest behind Rennala's arena for the Dark Moon Ring.
Beat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void - at the far end of the rot lake. Killing it unlocks the lift to the Moonlight Altar, provided the Dark Moon Ring is in your bag.
Beat Glintstone Dragon Adula (Moonlight Altar) - she guards the approach to the Cathedral of Manus Celes. Her drop is Adula's Moonblade, the 32 Intelligence cold sword-wave sorcery.

Get Dark Moon Greatsword - go into the Cathedral of Manus Celes, take the tunnel by the altar, and give Ranni the ring at the corpse of the Two Fingers. Around level 80 by now, with 38+ Intelligence to wield it.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King, seated on the Elden Throne itself.
Get Graven-Mass Talisman - in a chest at the top of the Albinauric Rise. Wear it alongside the Graven-School version; the two multiply.

Get Ranni's Dark Moon - Chelona's Rise, south-west of the Moonfolk Ruins. Three spirit turtles have to be shot: one near the tower, one on a ledge south-east of the Lunar Estate Ruins, one drifting over the evergaol portal to the north-west. Travel between them on foot or on Torrent or they will not appear.
Get Zamor Ice Storm - on a corpse against a wall in the southernmost quarter of the Zamor Ruins. 36 Intelligence, 17 FP, and it grinds 80 frostbite per tick out of a freezing tornado.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - level 125 is a comfortable place to be standing here.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the run ends at level 150 or so with Ranni's Dark Moon memorised and the greatsword buffed.

Reach Gravesite Plain - the first ground in the Land of Shadow. Before fighting anything, sweep it for Scadutree Fragments: two at the Church of Consolation, one beside Miquella's Cross at the Three-Path Cross grace, and one from a pot-carrying shadow in the Scorched Ruins graveyard.

Get Ash of War: Divine Beast Frost Stomp - clear Belurat, Tower Settlement, then trade the Dancing Lion's remembrance to Finger Reader Enia. It is a Cold affinity charging frost wave that works on almost every melee weapon.
Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight - inside Castle Ensis, on the road climbing out of Gravesite Plain toward Scadu Altus.

Get Rellana's Twinblade - trade her Remembrance of the Twin Moon Knight to Finger Reader Enia. It is a light greatsword at 8.0 weight with D scaling across the board and 103/66/66 physical, magic and fire damage.

Get Rellana's Twin Moons - the other half of the same remembrance, so duplicate at a Wandering Mausoleum coffin to take both. 72 Intelligence, 47 FP, 2 memory slots, and it drops two moons on a spot for enormous shockwave damage.

variants.name: The Cold Carian Knight
variants.twist: A pure Cold-infusion melee build that plays properly from level 20, decades before the Dark Moon Greatsword exists.
variants.notes: Buy the Glintstone Whetblade so you can put Cold affinity on a Carian Knight's Sword, which turns it into a magic-damage straight sword that scales off Intelligence and freezes on its own. Chilling Mist is the better ash here because it leaves the frost on the blade after the slash instead of on the floor. Carry the Carian Knight's Shield in the left hand through the Academy, where almost everything thrown at you is magic. It is a weaker ceiling than the greatsword but it carries the whole first half of the game and it lets you spend your early runes on Vigor instead of rushing 38 Intelligence.

variants.name: The Moon Sorcerer
variants.twist: Put the sword away and win from range with the two moons and a staff that boosts them.
variants.notes: The Carian Regal Scepter needs 60 Intelligence and pushes moon sorceries up by 10% when held, which covers both Ranni's Dark Moon and Rennala's Full Moon. Keep Carian Slicer memorised at 14 Intelligence and 4 FP as your panic button - it is fast enough to cancel out of and cheap enough to spam when a boss closes the gap. Black Knife Tiche is the better summon for a caster because she costs FP rather than 660 HP and her percentage-damage strikes give you the space to charge. If you go this way, trade a few points of Dexterity for Mind; you will run dry long before you run out of good targets.

variants.name: The Twin Moon Knight
variants.twist: A Shadow of the Erdtree finish that swaps the Carian moon for Rellana's, trading pure Intelligence for a split magic-and-fire weapon.
variants.notes: Rellana's weapon asks for 13 Strength, 16 Dexterity, 16 Intelligence and 16 Faith, and the base spread here runs 6 Faith, so this is a respec, not a pickup. At rune level 150 the working spread is 54 Vigor, 20 Mind, 20 Endurance, 16 Strength, 32 Dexterity, 62 Intelligence, 16 Faith, 9 Arcane. Be careful with the fire half of the weapon: fire damage clears frostbite the moment it lands, so apply your frost with Divine Beast Frost Stomp and then commit, rather than trying to freeze mid-combo. Remember Scadutree Blessing is what actually decides whether the DLC is fair - fragments raise it in twenty-one steps from 0 to 20, with the returns flattening around level 12, and none of it works outside the Land of Shadow.

pvp:
At the 125 and 150 meta brackets this build is a zoner that punishes anyone who dodges predictably.
Frostbite is one of the few statuses invaders cannot simply out-heal, and it still applies while a
target is in the invulnerability frames of a roll - they take the stagger and the negation penalty
even if the damage is skipped. Ranni's Dark Moon is the one to fear you for: it deletes incoming
sorceries in its path and cuts 10% of magic negation on hit. Note that the numbers shift against
players - Magic Scorpion Charm gives 8% magic damage but takes 15% more physical in PvP, and the
Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear drops from 20% to 12.5%. Avoid Lusat's Glintstone Staff in duels: the
50% extra FP per cast is fine against a boss and fatal against a human who can wait you out.
why:
Frostbite is a status effect, which in Elden Ring means a hidden meter that fills as you land
hits and then "procs" - fires once - when it reaches the top. Every enemy resists it with a
defensive stat called Robustness, so a heavily armoured knight takes longer to freeze than a
starved dog. What makes frostbite the engine of this build is what the proc actually does: it
deals damage equal to 10% of the target's maximum HP plus 30 on ordinary enemies (7% plus 30 on
bosses), and then lowers every one of their damage negation values by 20% for thirty seconds. Damage
negation is the percentage of incoming damage an enemy shrugs off, so cutting it means your
sword hits harder, your sorceries hit harder, and your summon's hits land harder too, for half
a minute, off one proc. Small humanoid enemies also get staggered when it goes off. The one
thing to remember is that fire wipes the debuff instantly, so do not pair frost with a fire
weapon on the same target.

The second half of the engine is that frost buildup is flat. Cold affinity - the infusion you
unlock with the Glintstone Whetblade - adds magic damage and Intelligence scaling to a weapon
and grants it frostbite, but that buildup number never scales with any of your stats. It is the
same whether you have 9 Arcane or 80. That is enormous for a build like this, because it means
every rune you spend can go into Intelligence and Dexterity for raw damage while the freezing
happens for free. It also means cheap, fast weapons are excellent frost applicators:
**Icerind Hatchet** carries 65 frost buildup at 3.0 weight and 16 Dexterity, and its locked
skill Hoarfrost Stomp lays a freezing carpet on the ground for 10 FP. You freeze with the cheap thing, then you
cash the window in with the expensive thing.

That expensive thing is the **Dark Moon Greatsword**. It wants 16 Strength, 11 Dexterity and 38
Intelligence, weighs 10.0, opens with D/D/C scaling in Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence, and
reaches a B in Intelligence at +5 on Somber Smithing Stones. It has 55 innate frostbite and its
skill, Moonlight Greatsword, is a self-buff for 32 FP that adds magic damage and gives your heavy
attacks a ranged moonlight wave. In practice you cast it once at the start of a fight, freeze
with a stomp or a cold sorcery, and then swing into a target whose negation is 20% lower for the
next thirty seconds. The talisman stack is built around making that window bigger:
**Graven-School Talisman** (+4% sorcery attack) and **Graven-Mass Talisman** (+8%) multiply
together rather than simply adding, **Magic Scorpion Charm** adds 12% magic damage at the cost of taking 10% more
physical, **Radagon Icon** grants 30 virtual Dexterity purely to shorten cast times, and
**Carian Filigreed Crest** cuts skill FP costs by 25% so Moonlight Greatsword and Hoarfrost Stomp
stop draining your bar.

Finally, the cold sorceries are their own little school and they have a hat. **Snow Witch Hat**
raises the damage of exactly four spells by 10%: Glintstone Icecrag, Adula's Moonblade, Zamor Ice
Storm and Ranni's Dark Moon - which is the whole cold list you will actually cast.
**Glintstone Icecrag** costs 12 FP at 15 Intelligence and puts 100 frostbite on a target, so it is your ranged opener
from level 25 onward. **Adula's Moonblade** at 32 Intelligence lands 120 frostbite on the
sweep and 35 on the projectile. **Ranni's Dark Moon**, the 68 Intelligence capstone, throws 270
frostbite and separately strips 10% of the target's magic negation, which stacks on top of the
20% the proc already took. That is the full loop: chill, proc, strip, delete.
firstHour:
Start as Prisoner - it opens at level 9 with 14 Dexterity and 14 Intelligence already in place,
plus a Glintstone Staff and the Magic Glintblade sorcery, which is exactly the pair of stats this
build spends the whole game raising. Clear the Cave of Knowledge tutorial, take the lift up to the
Stranded Graveyard, and get out onto the Limgrave overworld. Rest at the Church of Elleh, meet
Melina at the next grace to unlock Torrent, then come back to Elleh at night to find Ranni sitting
on the broken wall; she hands over the Spirit Calling Bell and the Lone Wolf Ashes, and three
summoned wolves solve most early-game crowding for free. Spend your first ten or twelve levels on
Vigor rather than damage - the Estoc you start with is a perfectly good weapon and dying is the
only thing that actually slows you down. Then ride north-west, cross into Liurnia of the Lakes,
and go straight for the Icerind Hatchet in the Temple Quarter tower; that single chest is where
the build starts being itself.

name: The Paladin
tagline: A holy knight whose sword drinks - buff up, swing hard, heal off every kill.
fantasy: You are the armored believer who fights in the front rank and never seems to run out of health bar. Every prayer you speak before a fight makes the next swing hit harder, and the sword you carry pays you back in life for every body it leaves behind. It is the least fragile way to play a Faith character, and the loudest.

route.text: Get Lordsworn's Greatsword - Gatefront Ruins, in the chest on the wagon a few steps south-east from the Gatefront grace.
Get Ash of War: Sacred Blade - dropped by a Scarab that crawls the slope beyond the pond, uphill and to the north-west from the Third Church of Marika.
Get Ash of War: Golden Vow - dropped by the mounted Godrick Knight on the rise northeast of the Warmaster's Shack in Stormhill.
Get Faith-knot Crystal Tear - in a stone bowl on the cliff edge north of the Demi-Human Forest Ruins, a short ride east from the Church of Pilgrimage, with Miranda Sprouts around it.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - on the gate bridge below Stormveil Castle.
Get Godslayer's Seal - Stormveil Castle, in a chest behind the fog wall in the rat cellar off the main courtyard, opened with one Stonesword Key.
Beat Godrick the Grafted, who waits in Stormveil Castle's throne room, at the very top of the keep.

Buy Lightning Spear - 6,000 runes from Miriel, Pastor of Vows at the Church of Vows, after you hand him the Dragon Cult Prayerbook, which a Leyndell Knight patrolling below the Artist's Shack carries.
Get Flame, Grant Me Strength - on a corpse against the eastern wall of Fort Gael, guarded by two Flame Chariots. You should reach level 40 around here.
Get Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear - from the miniboss at the Minor Erdtree down the cliffs northeast of the Smoldering Church.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the Wailing Dunes, entered through Redmane Castle once the festival is running.
Get Mimic Tear Ashes - in a chest behind an imp statue that needs one Stonesword Key.
Get Ash of War: Prayerful Strike - dropped by an invisible Scarab down in the Capital Outskirts moat, following it eastward from the Outer Wall Phantom Tree grace.
Get Golden Vow - inside the Corpse-Stench Shack, which sits off the Road of Iniquity a little way past the collapsed bridge.
Get Ritual Sword Talisman - in the cellar chest at Lux Ruins. You should reach level 80 around here.
Get Erdtree Seal - in an open cell northwest of the Prison Town Church grace inside Volcano Manor, with an Omenkiller nearby.
Beat Godskin Noble - the Temple of Eiglay, deep inside Volcano Manor.
Beat God-Devouring Serpent / Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy - at the far end of Volcano Manor, past Lady Tanith's drawing room.
Get Blasphemous Blade - warp to the Roundtable Hold and trade the Remembrance of the Blasphemous to Finger Reader Enia.

Get Coded Sword - up in the Fortified Manor, in the room that mirrors the chamber where the Roundtable's Two Fingers sit; the Sanctified Whetblade waits on the same level, at Smithing Master Hewg's empty seat. Both vanish once Maliketh dies.
Get Blessing of the Erdtree - a short walk from the Queen's Bedchamber grace. This one also disappears after Maliketh.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - at the Elden Throne. You should reach level 125 around here.
Beat Fire Giant - at the Forge of the Giants.
Get Shard of Alexander - accept Iron Fist Alexander's duel on the platform near the Dragon Temple Lift grace, after speaking to him in the Wailing Dunes and in the lava south of Fort Laiedd.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - at the top of the Dragon Temple.
Get Erdtree's Favor +2 - hanging from a tree root in the southern ash flats of Leyndell, Ashen Capital, past three Ulcerated Tree Spirits.
Beat Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Hoarah Loux) - in front of the Erdtree. You should reach level 150 around here.

Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - beneath the Erdtree; trade the Elden Remembrance afterwards for either the Sacred Relic Sword or Marika's Hammer, since one remembrance only buys one of them.
Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight - at the top of Castle Ensis, north across the plain.
Get Crusade Insignia - Fire Knight Queelign invades on the northwestern side of the Church of the Crusade, in the west of the plateau.
Get Two-Handed Sword Talisman - in a chest up the stairs past the Horned Warrior, in the tallest structure of the Temple Town Ruins.
Beat Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent) - at the top of the black keep.
Get Greatsword of Damnation - clear Midra's Manse, then hand the remembrance it yields to Finger Reader Enia.
Beat Promised Consort Radahn - at the Gate of Divinity.

routeNotes.text: The Land of Shadow opens only after you have killed Starscourge Radahn and Mohg, Lord of Blood; reach into the cocoon behind Mohg's arena, take hold of the withered arm, and you come round in a cave below the Church of Benediction. Scadutree Fragments are the real difficulty slider out here - there are 50 of them, and a full collection raises your damage by 200.5 percent and cuts incoming damage by 51.3 percent, but only inside the Land of Shadow. Hunt them before you complain that anything is too hard.

variants.name: The Lightning Prelate
variants.twist: Keep the armor and the front-line habits, but move the damage out of the sword and into your prayers, so bosses that punish melee can be fought from range.
variants.notes: Push Faith past the 40 target early and let Strength sit at 22, the minimum Blasphemous Blade asks for. Godfrey Icon adds 15 percent to charged sorceries, incantations and skills, and both lightning spears can be charged, so it replaces Shard of Alexander cleanly once you are casting more than swinging. Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear needs 32 Faith and costs 25 FP; it comes from the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook and sells for 8,500 runes. Take Faithful's Canvas Talisman from the corpse off the right-hand path in Sellia Crystal Tunnel for another 4 percent on incantation damage. Mind wants to be higher than the main build's, around 25 at level 150, because spear spam eats FP fast.

variants.name: The Golden Executioner
variants.twist: Trade lifesteal for reach and crowd control by making the Sacred Relic Sword the main hand and leaning on Wave of Gold to clear rooms in one press.
variants.notes: Sacred Relic Sword wants 14 Strength, 24 Dexterity and 22 Faith, and despite the halo it scales best with Dexterity, so this variant leans on the level-125 Dexterity target rather than pushing Strength to 30. Its damage is physical and holy, which is why the fire-boosting talisman and tear both get replaced by their holy equivalents - Sacred Scorpion Charm from the invader Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater outside the Smoldering Church, and Holy-Shrouding Cracked Tear from an Erdtree Avatar in Liurnia of the Lakes. Wave of Gold costs 42 FP and sweeps wide and slow, so it is a room-opener, not a duel-winner. Be aware that a lot of late-game enemies shrug off holy damage, so keep the Blasphemous Blade on your other weapon slot for those fights.

variants.name: The Crusader
variants.twist: A Shadow of the Erdtree finisher that swaps the stolen-life theme for scorched-earth aggression, rewarding you for killing fast rather than for killing safely.
variants.notes: Greatsword of Damnation needs 20 Strength, 15 Dexterity and 20 Faith - all of which the level-80 target already covers - and at 8.0 weight it is markedly lighter than the 13.5 of Blasphemous Blade, so you keep a medium roll in heavier armor. Crusade Insignia gives 15 percent attack power for 20 seconds after every kill, which turns any room full of Messmer soldiers into a rolling buff. Two-Handed Sword Talisman adds 15 percent to two-handed attacks, so commit to holding the sword in both hands and stop trying to use a shield. Because you lose the healing, this variant is the one that actually needs the Scadutree Blessing farmed up before the Shadow Keep. If you would rather cast than swing here, the Fire Knight's Seal sits behind the decapitated Marika statue in the largest church of the Shadow Keep, Church District, once the water is drained.

pvp: At the 125 and 150 meta levels this build arrives already legal - the level-125 spread is a normal duelling statline, and the level-150 one only adds Vigor and Faith. Expect the numbers to shrink: Golden Vow drops to 7.5 percent damage and 5 percent defence against players, Flame, Grant Me Strength drops to 15 percent, and Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman collapses from 20 percent to 5 percent, so do not build your plan around your buffs out-trading someone. Taker's Flames is a huge, slow, brightly-lit commitment that good players simply walk out of, so treat it as a punish for a whiffed heavy attack rather than an opener. One trap worth knowing if you run the Lightning Prelate variant: Godfrey Icon's bonus is bugged against other players for holy damage specifically and contributes nothing there, so keep it for the lightning spears, where it still pays.
why:
The engine of this build is one weapon and two prayers. The weapon is the **Blasphemous Blade**, the greatsword you get by trading Rykard's remembrance to Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold. Simply holding it in a hand you are actually using restores health equal to four percent of your maximum HP plus a flat 40 every time something dies near you. Its built-in skill, Taker's Flames, costs 30 FP, hits for roughly twice the weapon's own attack power, and refunds ten percent of whatever you hit plus another flat 150 health on contact. In plain terms: killing trash tops you up, and hitting a boss with the skill tops you up. You stop budgeting healing flasks and start budgeting aggression, which is why this is the friendliest Faith archetype for a first playthrough.

The two prayers are buffs, and they are different kinds of buff, which is exactly why they stack. **Golden Vow** is an aura buff - it radiates about six meters and covers you and any co-op partner, raising all damage you deal by 15 percent and cutting all damage you take by 10 percent for a very generous 80 seconds. **Flame, Grant Me Strength** is a body buff that only affects you, adding 20 percent to physical and fire attack power and speeding up stamina recovery, but it burns out after 30 seconds. Because the game files them under separate categories they multiply together rather than overwriting each other. Blasphemous Blade deals physical and fire damage and nothing else, so Flame, Grant Me Strength boosts every point of it. Cast Golden Vow first while you are walking to the fog wall, then Flame, Grant Me Strength as the last thing before you step through, and open with Taker's Flames.

Faith does two jobs here, and it is worth knowing which is which. Blasphemous Blade's Faith scaling only feeds the smaller fire half of its damage, so Faith is technically its weakest stat per point for raw weapon attack - the wiki's own comparison puts a pure-Faith setup about six percent behind on weapon attack power, but twelve percent ahead on skill attack power. Since Taker's Flames is where most of your damage and all of your healing comes from, that trade is worth taking. Faith's second job is the seal. A sacred seal is the catalyst you need to cast incantations at all, and its "incantation scaling" number is what actually decides how hard your prayers hit. **Godslayer's Seal** needs 27 Faith and is the strongest Faith-only seal from there up to 68 Faith; **Erdtree Seal** needs 40 Faith and overtakes it above that, going from 212 incantation scaling at 40 Faith to 353 at 80 Faith when fully upgraded. Erdtree Seal also upgrades with the much easier Somber Smithing Stones, which is why the level-125 target parks Faith exactly at 40.

Talismans finish the loop. **Shard of Alexander** adds 15 percent to the attack power of skills, which is a direct 15 percent on Taker's Flames. **Ritual Sword Talisman** adds 10 percent attack power while your health bar is completely full - normally a fussy condition, but a sword that refills you after every kill keeps you pinned at full more often than any other build in the game. **Fire Scorpion Charm** adds 12 percent fire attack at the cost of taking 10 percent more physical damage, a bargain you can afford behind Golden Vow's damage reduction. Round it out with **Erdtree's Favor +2** for health, stamina and carry weight, and **Great-Jar's Arsenal** - won by beating the three duellists the Great Jar summons in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow - for another 19 percent equip load, so you can wear real armor instead of rags. For a fight that hits like a truck, swap Fire Scorpion Charm out for **Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman** and its flat 20 percent physical damage reduction.
firstHour: Pick Confessor and take the Golden Seed as your keepsake; you start with a Finger Seal, a Broadsword, a Blue Crest Heater Shield and enough Faith to cast, which saves you a dozen levels of catch-up. Clear the tutorial cave, ride out to the Church of Elleh, buy a Crafting Kit from Merchant Kale, then head north up the road to Gatefront Ruins and open the wagon chest for the Lordsworn's Greatsword. Detour northwest of the Third Church of Marika for the Scarab that drops Ash of War: Sacred Blade, and take it to any site of grace to put the Sacred affinity on the greatsword - the Sacred affinity gives up part of a weapon's physical damage in return for holy damage and a Faith scaling letter, which turns a plain soldier's sword into a real Faith weapon on day one. Then double back to Stormhill for the mounted knight who drops Ash of War: Golden Vow, and put that on a light backup weapon rather than your main, so you can swap to it, cast the buff and swap back without giving up Sacred Blade. Spend your first levels on Vigor until it reads 20, and only then start feeding Faith.

name: The Plague Doctor
tagline: Stack rot, poison and bleed until the boss dies of its own wounds.
fantasy: You do not out-trade anything. You touch it once, twice, and then you walk backwards while three separate meters drain its health for you. Every fight becomes a clock you started and the boss cannot stop.

route.text: Leave the Cave of Knowledge as a Bandit with the Stonesword Key keepsake - the keepsake hands you two keys, which is exactly the toll on the gate in step 2.

Get the Dragon Communion Seal - Fringefolk Hero's Grave, straight down from the Stranded Graveyard; spend both Stonesword Keys on the gate, take the ramps down and right, and kill the spectral Banished Knight in the side chamber. Skip the dungeon boss, you only want the seal.
Kill Flying Dragon Agheel - he lands in the shallow water at Agheel Lake; ride Torrent in circles and hit his feet. He pays out the Dragon Heart you need next.
Get Poison Mist - a scarab carries it near the poisoned water east of the road to Castle Morne, south of the Castle Morne Rampart grace. Shoot it before it burrows.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gatehouse below Stormveil Castle. Poison Mist under his feet plus your dagger is a legitimate answer at this level.
Beat Godrick the Grafted inside Stormveil Castle, at the throne room crowning the keep.
Get Ash of War: Poisonous Mist - a teleporting scarab on the small island south-east of the Aeonia Swamp Shore grace, out in the Swamp of Aeonia.

Buy Rotten Breath - the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in southern Caelid takes one Dragon Heart for it. Level 40 is the marker for the end of the early game, and it is enough to hold 20 Dexterity, 15 Faith and 17 Arcane.

Kill Commander O'Neil - he stands in the deep rot of the Swamp of Aeonia with a squad of Cleanrot Knights; kill the squad first from horseback. He drops the Unalloyed Gold Needle that opens Millicent's questline.

Get the Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom - take the needle to Sage Gowry at Gowry's Shack north of Sellia Gateway, deliver the repaired needle to Millicent at the Church of the Plague, rest, then go back to Gowry.

Get the Venomous Fang - on a corpse inside the Abandoned Cave, reached by the root bridge east of the Smoldering Wall grace. Grab the Serpent Bow in the same cave; it needs 8 Strength, 15 Dexterity and 11 Arcane and adds 15 Poison to every arrow.
Kill Decaying Ekzykes - the rot-eaten dragon that patrols the dragon fields west of Sellia. Two more Dragon Hearts is the point of the fight.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the library at the bottom of Raya Lucaria Academy. She becomes your respec NPC, which matters here because this build lives on exact stat breakpoints.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the festival at Redmane Castle drops you into the Wailing Dunes; summon everyone. His death shakes open the way underground.

Get the Black Whetblade - on a corpse beside the altar at Night's Sacred Ground, overlooking the huge silver tear. This is the item that unlocks Poison, Blood and Occult affinities. Pick up the Mimic Tear Ashes from the Stonesword Key chest nearby while you are here.

Beat Elemer of the Briar - the top of The Shaded Castle in the poisoned mire of northern Altus. The Valkyrie's Prosthesis sits in a chest inside; hand it to Millicent, which unlocks Pest Threads from Gowry for 7,500 runes.

Get the Antspur Rapier - Maleigh Marais, Shaded Castle Castellan wanders the broken ground west of the castle alongside a Guardian Golem. Kill him, take the rapier, put a Poison affinity on it at any blacksmith.
Get Kindred of Rot's Exultation - clear Seethewater Cave on the north-eastern flank of the mountain and kill the pair of Kindred of Rot at the bottom.
Get the Serpentbone Blade - Tanith hands it over at Volcano Manor once you complete the Rileigh the Idle contract. It needs 22 Dexterity and inflicts Deadly Poison.
Beat Godskin Apostle (Altus Plateau) - the arena under Dominula, Windmill Village; summon Millicent for it and talk to her afterwards. Level 80 is the marker for the end of the mid game.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the throne at the top of the capital.

Get Scorpion's Stinger - follow the Ainsel River down to the lake, then take the chest in the small shrine west of the Grand Cloister grace, guarded by Kindred of Rot. It cannot be infused or re-skilled, so it stays a clean 50-rot dagger forever. Take the Mushroom Crown off the corpse on the pillar in the ruins to the south-east.

Get Ash of War: Seppuku - an invisible scarab on the northern shore of the frozen lake, across from the First Church of Marika. Put it on the Antspur Rapier and keep the Poison affinity for the three-status combo.
Get the Thorny Cracked Tear - the Putrid Avatar at the Minor Erdtree east of Ordina, Liturgical Town drops it.
Meet Millicent at the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins - exhaust her dialogue before you set foot in the Haligtree or you lose the reward in step 26.

Get the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia - in Elphael, find Millicent by the Prayer Room grace, kill the Putrid Tree Spirit past it, then take the gold summon sign on the ledge above the rot pool and help her fight her four sisters.
Beat Malenia, Blade of Miquella - the root chamber at the bottom of Elphael. Her remembrance trades with Finger Reader Enia for the Scarlet Aeonia incantation.

Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - the ruined dome in the storm. Finish Iron Fist Alexander here first for the Shard of Alexander, which adds 15% to skill damage and therefore to Poisonous Mist.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the Erdtree throne after the capital burns. You want to be between level 125 and 150 walking in.

Beat Mohg, Lord of Blood - the palace under the Consecrated Snowfield portal. With Radahn already dead, touching the withered arm in the Cocoon of the Empyrean beside his arena drops you into the Gravesite Plain.

Get the Poisoned Hand - in Belurat, Tower Settlement, north-west of the Main Gate Cross grace: take the Well Depths Key from the room past the covered bridge, open the grating at the bottom of the well, and follow the sewer to the north edge of the poison swamp. It needs 28 Arcane and buffs your attack when anything nearby is poisoned or rotting.
Get Ash of War: The Poison Flower Blooms Twice - a teardrop scarab sits in the small rot pool south of the Ravine North grace, past the river and near the ruins under the big bridge.
Get Pest-Thread Spears - on a corpse at the bottom of the stairs by the Church of the Bud, around to the left. It needs 26 Faith, so treat it as a respec option rather than a default.

Beat Romina, Saint of the Bud - the Church of the Bud. She rots you with her poleblade, so bring the immunity gear you have been ignoring. Her remembrance trades for the Rotten Butterflies incantation.

variants.name: The Dragon Cultist
variants.twist: Drop most of the melee and fill rot meters entirely from range with dragon breath.
variants.notes: Ekzykes's Decay costs two Dragon Hearts at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion once Decaying Ekzykes is dead, and it lands up to three hits of 65 Scarlet Rot per breath with two breaths per cast. It asks for 23 Faith and 15 Arcane, so respec at Rennala and pull the extra Faith out of Dexterity - you are barely swinging a weapon in this version anyway. Keep 48 FP free before every boss opener. This is the most forgiving way to play the archetype and the safest against anything with a long reach.

variants.name: The Bloodfly
variants.twist: Run a second Arcane ailment alongside the rot so two meters are always close to popping.
variants.notes: Reduvia is a dagger needing 5 Strength, 13 Dexterity and 13 Arcane with 50 blood loss, and it drops from a Limgrave invasion very early, so this version comes online long before the Antspur Rapier does. Swarm of Flies needs 11 Faith and 16 Arcane and its blood loss scales with Arcane when you cast it off the Dragon Communion Seal. Lord of Blood's Exultation gives +20% attack for 20 seconds when anything within 7 metres bleeds, which is the same shape of bonus as Kindred of Rot's Exultation on a different trigger - run both and your buff bar never goes dark. Note that it falls to +12% against other players.

variants.name: The Antspur Duelist
variants.twist: One weapon, three ailments, and a talisman set built to punish the second someone tips over.
variants.notes: Keep the Poison affinity on the rapier and put Seppuku on top of it. Seppuku costs you a chunk of health to stain the blade, and in exchange you get an attack boost and blood loss buildup for the duration, on a weapon that already carries innate rot and affinity poison. Millicent's Prosthesis is the betrayal reward from her questline: +5 Dexterity plus 4%, 6% and 11% on successive attacks. Taking it means you never get the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, so pick one and commit. Scorpion's Stinger in the off-hand exists purely so a single dagger poke can top up a rot meter that is one hit short.

pvp:
At the 125 and 150 metas this build is genuinely oppressive and genuinely hated, because rot and
poison do not care about your opponent's poise or their heals - a healed opponent with a full rot
meter is still losing the fight. Play it patient: poke with the Antspur Rapier, disengage, and let
the timers work rather than trying to win a trade you were never built to win. What changes from
PvE is that several of your multipliers are cut against players - Lord of Blood's Exultation drops
from 20% to 12%, and the Poisoned Hand's buff drops from 7.5% to 5% - so do not build your damage
plan around them holding up. Avoid the long-cast incantations entirely; Rotten Breath and Poison
Mist are read and rolled by anyone competent, and the recovery frames get you killed. At 150 you
can afford 60 Vigor and enough Endurance for a medium roll, which is the correct trade in duels.
why:
Every enemy in the game carries a set of invisible meters, one per ailment. Hitting them with an
attack that carries Scarlet Rot fills the rot meter; hitting them with poison fills a different
meter. When a meter fills, the ailment fires and the target starts losing health on a timer that
runs whether you are anywhere near it or not. The meters drain back down if you stop applying
them, and the target's Immunity stat decides how much you need to pour in before it tips over.
The important part for this build is that the meters are separate. Scarlet Rot and Poison do not
share a bar, so a single weapon can be filling both at once, and a third meter can be filling on
top of that. That is the whole design: you are not trying to win a damage race, you are trying to
get three timers running and then survive them.

The engine is the Antspur Rapier. It is a Thrusting Sword that needs 10 Strength and 20 Dexterity,
weighs 3, and carries 55 Scarlet Rot on every hit. That 55 is fixed - it does not grow with your
Arcane, and it does not grow when you upgrade the weapon, so it is exactly as strong at +1 as it
is at +25. What you can change is everything around it. Once you have the Black Whetblade you can
put a Poison affinity on the rapier, which layers poison buildup on top of the rot and makes both
the poison buildup and the physical damage scale off Arcane. Then you put Ash of War: Seppuku on
it, which stains the blade with your own blood for a temporary attack boost and blood loss buildup.
Rot from the weapon, poison from the affinity, blood loss from the skill: three meters filling from
one combo. If you prefer, Ash of War: Poisonous Mist plus a Blood affinity reaches the same place
from the other direction.

The talismans turn your own damage-over-time into a damage buff, which is why this build hits far
harder than the raw attack numbers suggest. Kindred of Rot's Exultation gives +20% attack power for
20 seconds whenever anything within 7 metres is suffering Poison or Scarlet Rot. Mushroom Crown
gives another +10% on the same trigger, and it counts you as well, so standing in your own poison
cloud keeps it lit. Rotten Winged Sword Insignia adds 6%, then 8%, then 13% as you land successive
hits, and Thorny Cracked Tear in your Flask of Wondrous Physick stacks a separate consecutive-attack
bonus of up to 20% for three minutes. None of these are conditional on a hard-to-hit setup - the
condition is simply "you are doing the thing this build already does", so all of them are up almost
all the time.

Ranged application is what makes the whole thing safe against bosses. Rotten Breath needs 15 Faith
and 12 Arcane, costs 36 FP, and applies up to 65 Scarlet Rot per hit with up to three hits per
breath, which fills most rot meters in a single cast from outside melee range. Poison Mist needs
only 12 Faith and pours 100 Poison per second for 16 seconds into a small cloud - drop it under a
boss, walk away, and the meter fills without you taking a swing. Cast both off the Dragon Communion
Seal, which requires 10 Faith and 10 Arcane, scales C in Arcane, and boosts Dragon Communion
incantations by 15%. That is why the stat spread parks Faith at exactly 15 and pushes everything
else into Dexterity and Arcane: 15 Faith is the price of admission for the two spells that matter,
and every point past it is wasted. For reference on what you are buying, standard poison deals
0.07% of the target's maximum HP plus 7 damage per second for 90 seconds; the Deadly Poison carried
by weapons like Serpentbone Blade hits harder at 0.14% plus 14 per second but only runs 30 seconds.
Be aware that some late bosses have enormous Immunity and will never tip over - keep a real weapon
upgraded so you always have a plan B.
firstHour:
Start as a Bandit and take the Stonesword Key keepsake, which gives you two keys - exactly the toll
on the sealed gate in Fringefolk Hero's Grave. Walk out of the Cave of Knowledge, ignore the Tree
Sentinel on the road, and go straight back down to that gate to steal the Dragon Communion Seal off
the spectral Banished Knight; the chariot in the corridor will do most of the work if you bait it.
Your Great Knife carries you through Limgrave fine, so spend the first levels on Vigor and just
enough Faith and Arcane to hold the seal at 10 and 10. Kill Flying Dragon Agheel at Agheel Lake for
your first Dragon Heart, then ride south to the Weeping Peninsula and shoot the scarab near the
Castle Morne road for Poison Mist. From that point on you have a spell that wins fights you have no
business winning, and the rest of the build is just adding meters to it.

name: The Ronin
tagline: One katana, one stance, one clean opening - the honest swordsman of the Lands Between.
fantasy: You are a swordsman from a country nobody here has heard of, carrying a curved blade nobody here knows how to fight. You do not out-muscle anything and you do not out-range anything; you wait one beat longer than the boss expects, step through the swing, and open a wound that keeps bleeding while you back away. It is the most patient way to play Elden Ring and the one that makes you feel like you actually learned the game.

route.text: Get Whetstone Knife - Gatefront Ruins, in the cellar chest under the ruins by the first big road grace.
Get Ash of War: Unsheathe - from a scarab standing in the water at the southeastern corner of Agheel Lake.
Get Bloodhound's Fang - Forlorn Hound Evergaol in southern Limgrave; Blaidd the Half-Wolf can be summoned to help.
Get Uchigatana - Deathtouched Catacombs, west of Saintsbridge in northern Stormhill, on a hidden ledge behind an illusory wall.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gate below Stormveil Castle. He takes 10% extra from slash damage and bleeds readily, so keep the katana chain going.
Get Claw Talisman - Stormveil Castle, out on the rooftops reached from the Rampart Tower grace; it adds 15% to jump attacks.
Get Iron Whetblade - Stormveil Castle, in the imp-sealed room off the courtyard beside the elevator back to Rampart Tower.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the graveyard arena at the top of Stormveil Castle. His bleed resistance is among the lowest of any main boss. Level target for the end of this act: 40.
Get Winged Sword Insignia - at the bottom of Stillwater Cave.
Get Glintstone Whetblade - Academy of Raya Lucaria, Debate Parlor, on a corpse in the room below two sorcerers.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the grand library of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. From now on she will rebuild your stats for one Larval Tear, so mistakes below are reversible.
Beat Starscourge Radahn - the Wailing Dunes, reached through the festival at Redmane Castle. Ignore bleed here and win on spacing.
Get Mimic Tear Ashes - in a chest behind an imp statue that costs one Stonesword Key. It copies your gear, so it fights with a katana too.
Get Black Whetblade - Night's Sacred Ground, on a corpse by the altar looking down on a giant silver tear.
Get Nagakiba - lying beside the dying Yura at the Second Church of Marika, northwest of the Altus Highway Junction; you must have met him in Limgrave and at the Academy gate first.
Get Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step - from the Night's Cavalry that patrols the easternmost bridge of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow after dark.
Get Lord of Blood's Exultation - Leyndell Catacombs, beneath the capital.
Beat Godfrey, First Elden Lord - the golden apparition inside the Erdtree Sanctuary. Level target for the end of this act: 80.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King - the throne room at the top of the capital.
Get Dragonscale Blade - raise the walkway with the nearby pillars first so you spend less time standing in the rot.
Get Ash of War: Seppuku - carried by an invisible scarab on the northern shore of the Frozen Lake, opposite the First Church of Marika.
Beat Fire Giant - Flame Peak. He has negative slash resistance, so a katana is the right tool; strike the wounded ankle in phase one.
Get Thorny Cracked Tear - from the miniboss at the Minor Erdtree east of Ordina, Liturgical Town.
Get Shard of Alexander - finish Iron Fist Alexander in the northwest of the ruins and speak to him afterwards; it adds 15% to skill damage.
Beat Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade - keep the Blasphemous Claw on your belt to deflect his black-blade swing.
Get Rotten Winged Sword Insignia - take the gold summon sign in Elphael after the Putrid Tree Spirit and fight beside Millicent against her sisters.

Beat Malenia, Blade of Miquella - past the Haligtree Roots grace. Bleed and frost both stagger her, and she heals off every blow she lands even on your guard. Level target for the end of this act: 125.
Get Hand of Malenia - hand her Remembrance of the Rot Goddess to Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold; it needs 48 Dexterity.
Beat Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Hoarah Loux) - the Ashen Capital. Run, do not roll, when he cracks the ground after his leap.
Beat Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast - the last fight. Level target: 150.
Get Dragon-Hunter's Great Katana - at the far end of the Dragon's Pit. It is the cheapest way to try the DLC's new great katana class.
Get Rellana's Cameo - Castle Ensis, on an altar directly behind Moonrithyll, Carian Knight; it adds 45% to stance skills such as Unsheathe once you have held the stance a second.
Get Rakshasa's Great Katana - the Eastern Nameless Mausoleum on the bank of the Recluses' River.
Beat Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent) - you need his Kindling to burn the Sealing Tree and open the rest of the expansion.
Beat Promised Consort Radahn, waiting at the summit past the Gate of Divinity.

variants.name: Bleeding Ronin
variants.twist: Give up a slice of raw sword damage to make the haemorrhage meter fill roughly twice as fast, then open every fight by stabbing yourself.
variants.notes: Ash of War: Seppuku puts the Blood affinity on the weapon, and its skill raises both your attack power and your blood loss buildup for a while at the cost of a chunk of your own health - so cast it before you walk through the fog, not during the fight. Blood affinity moves part of the weapon's scaling onto Arcane, so a pure Dexterity Ronin loses a little attack power here; you are buying speed of proc, not size of hit. Lord of Blood's Exultation then pays you 20% attack power for 20 seconds every time anything nearby bleeds, including yourself, so Seppuku turns it on for free. This is the variant for Godrick, Margit, Morgott and Malenia, and the wrong variant for Starscourge Radahn.

route.text: Get Black Whetblade - this is now mandatory, not optional: it is what unlocks the Blood affinity at a Site of Grace.
Get Ash of War: Seppuku - move this pickup as early as you can bear; the whole variant is offline until you have it.

variants.name: Frostbite Ronin
variants.twist: Trade bleed for frost, which slows the target, raises the damage it takes, and works on the many late-game enemies that resist haemorrhage.
variants.notes: Ash of War: Chilling Mist applies the Cold affinity, which the Glintstone Whetblade unlocks; Cold adds magic damage and Intelligence scaling on top of frost buildup, so on a 9-Intelligence Ronin you take it purely for the frostbite. Pair it with the Dragonscale Blade, whose own Ice Lightning Sword skill coats the blade in lightning and adds 80 frostbite buildup, so both hands are filling the same meter. The Dragonscale Blade cannot be infused or buffed, so it stays in your off-hand slot as the frost applicator while the infused Nagakiba does the killing. Frost is the better answer to Crumbling Farum Azula and to Malenia's second phase.

variants.name: Great Katana Ronin (Shadow of the Erdtree)
variants.twist: Put down the katana for its bigger cousin - a two-handed weapon class added by the expansion that keeps the bleed but swings with real weight behind it.
variants.notes: Rakshasa's Great Katana asks for 27 Dexterity, carries 55 blood loss buildup and gives you poise while you attack, but it also strips 10% off all your damage negation, so it rewards the player who has already stopped panic-rolling. It cannot be infused and upgrades with Somber Smithing Stones, which means one stone line instead of nine. The Bloodsucking Cracked Tear is the matching flask piece: a flat 20% more damage for three minutes while it quietly drains your health, which is a fair trade on a build that ends fights quickly. Bring the Strength target at level 150 up to 30 before you commit, and keep the Dragon-Hunter's Great Katana around for the expansion's several dragons.

route.text: Get Great Katana - on a corpse in the lake of the northern Gravesite Plain, west of the Abandoned Ailing Village where the Ghostflame Dragon roams; take this before Rakshasa's so you can learn the class on something replaceable.

pvp:
Build for 125 first and 150 only if your friends invade at that ceiling; those are the two levels where
you will actually find people. Katanas are strong in duels for the same reason they are strong on
bosses - the bleed proc staggers other players and takes 15% of their health, and a Seppuku-buffed
Nagakiba reaches further than most opponents read. Expect the numbers to shrink: Lord of Blood's
Exultation gives 12% instead of 20% against players, the Claw Talisman gives 7.5% instead of 15%, and
the Bloodsucking Cracked Tear gives 12.5% instead of 20%. Bloodhound's Step is the real prize and the
real tell - it is fast, it briefly hides you, and everyone who duels knows the animation, so spend it
to escape a committed swing rather than to open with it. Avoid leading with the Unsheathe skill in an
even fight; it is a stance with a long tell that good players simply walk around.
why:
The Ronin is built on one number that most new players never look at: blood loss buildup. A katana
does not just deal damage when it lands, it also fills a hidden meter on whatever you hit. The
Uchigatana you start with adds 45 points to that meter per hit and the Nagakiba adds the same, while
the Hand of Malenia adds 50. When the meter fills, the target haemorrhages: it takes a flat lump of
damage plus a slice of its own maximum health at once, and most human-sized enemies are staggered
while it happens. The flat portion is 100 on an ordinary bleed weapon; the percentage portion is 15%
of maximum health on normal enemies and other players, and 10.5% on bosses and their companions. That
is why a katana that looks weak on paper kills a giant boss faster than a slab of a greatsword. You
are not out-damaging its health bar, you are billing it a percentage of that bar every few seconds.

The meter also decays. If you poke once and run away, the buildup drains and you have accomplished
nothing. So the whole build is arranged around getting three or four hits in a row instead of one. The
Uchigatana's light attack chain is fast enough to do that inside a single opening, and the two
talismans that reward exactly that behaviour are the Winged Sword Insignia and later the Rotten Winged
Sword Insignia: both give you a stacking attack-power bonus for landing successive attacks, the base
version topping out around 10% and the rotten version around 13%. Millicent's Prosthesis does the same
thing and hands you five free Dexterity on top. Add the Thorny Cracked Tear in your Flask of Wondrous
Physick (the reusable flask you mix two Crystal Tears into at a Site of Grace, one charge per rest)
and that same successive-attack counter is worth up to another 20% for three minutes. None of these
are conditional on a boss being at low health or on you being at full HP - they are conditional on you
committing to a combo, which is the exact habit that makes you good at this game.

Dexterity is the stat that pays for all of it. It is the attribute most katanas scale with, meaning
each point of DEX adds attack power to the weapon in proportion to that weapon's scaling letter (E is
a small return, C is a fair one, B is good, S is best). The Uchigatana starts at D in both Strength and
Dexterity, the Nagakiba at D Strength and C Dexterity, and the Hand of Malenia reaches B Dexterity when
fully upgraded. If you want more of that return, apply the Keen affinity with the Iron Whetblade: Keen
trades away part of the Strength contribution to push Dexterity scaling higher, which is a straight
profit on a build that is never going above 30 Strength. Iron Whetblade also unlocks Heavy (Strength
biased) and Quality (both), so it is the single most useful pickup in Stormveil Castle for this build.

The rest is survivability and honesty about what this build cannot do. Vigor is your health and it is
the only stat that stops a one-shot, which is why the level checkpoints below climb it hard before
they finish Dexterity. Endurance is stamina and equip load, and equip load decides whether you keep
the fast dodge roll - a Ronin who armours up into a slow roll has thrown away the entire point of the
build. Mind is FP, the resource your Ash of War skills spend, and you need very little of it because
Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step costs only 5 FP a use. Finally, be honest about bleed's limits: some
bosses shrug it off. Starscourge Radahn's bleed resistance is enormous and climbs every time the meter
fills, so that fight is won with plain sword damage and spacing, not with haemorrhage. Godrick the
Grafted, Margit and Malenia sit at the other end - all three take bleed badly, and Malenia in
particular is staggered by it, which is the single most useful fact in the endgame for this build.
firstHour:
Drop into the tutorial cave under the Stranded Graveyard, kill the Soldier of Godrick at the end of
it, and take the free lesson on rolling - the Samurai's whole life is timing, and you already own the
best starting weapon in the game for it. Surface, ride out to the Church of Elleh, and take the
Whetstone Knife from the cellar chest at Gatefront Ruins so you can start changing skills at a Site of
Grace. Ride south to the Forlorn Hound Evergaol for Bloodhound's Fang, which will carry you through
anything in Limgrave that your Uchigatana cannot. Then walk the ravine north of Agheel Lake towards
Murkwater Cave, meet Yura, and let him fight the invader who shows up - that handshake is the first
step of the questline that eventually hands you the Nagakiba, and it is easy to walk past forever.
Put your first ten levels into Vigor, not Dexterity; the Uchigatana is already strong enough, and what
kills new Ronin is a health bar, not a damage number.
