name: The Pure Sorcerer
tagline: Glintstone staff, Comet Azur, deletion at range - and a body made of glass.
fantasy: You stand at the far end of the arena and take things apart before they reach you. A staff in one hand, a memory full of comets, and a physick flask that turns one boss fight into a ten-second beam of starlight. Nothing survives your opening if you set it up right, and nothing forgives you if something closes the gap.

route.text: Reach The First Step - the cliffside grace above the coast, out past the tutorial cave; the armoured thing inside is meant to kill you the first time.

Find Waypoint Ruins Cellar - the sunken stairway inside the ruins east of Agheel Lake; Sorceress Sellen sits below it and becomes your first spell shop, and her Royal House Scroll stock unlocks Carian Slicer for 1,500 runes once you fetch the scroll from the ruined building on the hill east of the Agheel Lake South grace.

Take Meteorite Staff - ride the trap chest inside Dragon-Burnt Ruins to Sellia Crystal Tunnel, touch the grace there so you can warp out again, then walk west into the Swamp of Aeonia to the broken tower at the south-west edge of Street of Sages Ruins.
Take Rock Sling - a chest in the cellar of those same ruins, a few steps from the staff.
Take Ambush Shard - the corpse beside the caged sorceress in the Witchbane Ruins cellar, in the poison pool south of the Fourth Church of Marika.
Take Lhutel the Headless - the shade at the bottom of Tombsward Catacombs drops her, and a summon that holds attention is worth more to you than any weapon.
Beat Margit, the Fell Omen - the gate at the top of Stormhill; Rock Sling chips his stance where your glintstone barely does, so open at range and reset every time he closes.
Beat Godrick the Grafted - the throne room at the end of Stormveil Castle.
Buy Great Glintstone Shard - hand Sellen the Academy Scroll from the graveyard west of the Land-Facing Cliffs grace, then pay her 2,000 runes; this replaces Glintstone Pebble as your default poke.
Take Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear - the avatar at the north-eastern Minor Erdtree drops it alongside its lightning and holy siblings.
Take Radagon Icon - from the Debate Parlour grace go out into the courtyard, right around the building, over the fence, up a ladder and in through a broken window to the chest on the landing.
Take Comet - a corpse tucked behind an illusory wall near the Debate Parlour entrance; you cannot cast it until 52 Intelligence, so bank it.

Take Graven-School Talisman - in the room west of Debate Parlour, strike the empty bookshelf on the north side, climb the ladder beyond it, vault the railing by the leaning painting and drop through the hole onto the crystal pile.
Take Terra Magicus - two Stonesword Keys open Academy Crystal Cave; past the boss a lift runs up to the academy belfry and the chest at the top.
Beat Red Wolf of Radagon - the hall past the Schoolhouse Classroom grace, and the only thing between you and the library.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon - the Raya Lucaria Grand Library; lead with Rock Sling and your summon, because her magic resistance is 80 and her physical resistance is not.
Claim Carian Regal Scepter - carry the Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen to Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold; it needs 60 Intelligence, so it waits in your box for a while.

Take Azur's Glintstone Staff - from Debate Parlour head out to the left past two sorcerers, drop to the stairs, cross onto the academy rooftops, take the ladder at their end, then enter the domed structure through a window and cross the enclosed bridge past the High Page.
Take Night Comet - light the brazier in the south-western tower of Sellia, Town of Sorcery to drop the barrier around the chest in the middle of town.
Take Lusat's Glintstone Staff - the chest waiting past the Nox pair in the same town.
Take Crystal Torrent - the three of them at the bottom of Sellia Hideaway, the cave hidden behind an illusory cliff face north-east of the town.
Take Comet Azur - Primeval Sorcerer Azur is fossilised on the cliffs south-east of Hermit Village, and simply speaking to him hands it over.
Take Cerulean Hidden Tear - the tree spirit at the Minor Erdtree south of the Road of Iniquity grace drops it.
Take Stars of Ruin - show Sellen the sorcery you took from Azur and she gives you the Sellian Sealbreaker; use it on the barrier deep in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Primeval Sorcerer Lusat.
Take Godfrey Icon - a Stonesword Key activates the Golden Lineage Evergaol in the south-west corner of the plateau.
Take Ritual Sword Talisman - the chest in the cellar of Lux Ruins, in the south-west of the plateau.

Take Mimic Tear Ashes - beat Starscourge Radahn to open the crater, then break the imp statue guarding the chest with Stonesword Keys; the copy it summons costs health rather than FP and casts everything you can.
Take Ranni's Dark Moon - once Ranni's questline opens the Moonlight Altar, wake the three spectral turtles on foot and enter Chelona's Rise from the Altar South grace.
Take Graven-Mass Talisman - turn the phantom imps outside Albinauric Rise on each other to unseal the door, then open the chest at the top.
Take Mass of Putrescence - drop to the ledge below the Fissure Waypoint grace; it needs 22 Faith as well as 28 Intelligence, so it is a side option rather than a core pick.
Take Rings of Spectral Light - head east from the grace and climb onto the arch toward the Death Rite Bird; six rings of ghostflame that stack frostbite, again gated behind 18 Faith.

Buy Glintstone Nail - Count Ymir sells it at the Cathedral of Manus Metyr for 12,000 runes once you have rung the bell at the Finger Ruins of Rhia; at 10 FP and 18 Intelligence it is the cheapest strong repeat cast in the game.
Take Staff of the Great Beyond - trade the Remembrance of the Mother of Fingers to Enia; it is the only catalyst that casts sorceries and incantations both, at 25 Intelligence and 25 Faith.
Claim Rellana's Twin Moons - Enia converts the remembrance from the fight past the Castle Ensis Checkpoint grace; 72 Intelligence and two memory slots for the single loudest sorcery in the expansion.

routeNotes.text: Early (target: level 40 by the end of Stormveil)
Mid (target: level 80 by the end of Caelid)
Late (target: level 125 through Leyndell, 150 by the end)

variants.name: Starfall Battery
variants.twist: Build the whole character around one ten-second window, then walk away from bosses you were never supposed to beat yet.
variants.notes: The order matters more than the numbers. Summon your spirit, cast **Terra Magicus** at your feet, drink the physick holding **Cerulean Hidden Tear** and **Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear**, then start the beam and do not move. The tear zeroes FP for ten seconds and the sigil lasts thirty, so you have room to reposition once and beam again on the flask's magic bonus alone. **Godfrey Icon** is dead weight in this variant, since the beam is held rather than charged; the **Magic Scorpion Charm** replaces it and pays for its extra physical damage taken with 12 percent more magic. Keep three memory slots free, because the beam eats all three by itself.

variants.name: The Unseen Sniper
variants.twist: Trade raw scaling for spells the enemy never reacts to, and pick fights from outside their awareness.
variants.notes: A **Staff of Loss** lifts **Night Comet** and **Night Shard** by 30 percent when held, and by 69 percent if you can get a second one in the other hand. Note the trap: **Ambush Shard** is a night sorcery too but the staff does nothing for it, so keep it for the shot that curls around a shield rather than for damage. Non-player enemies do not dodge night sorceries at all, which makes long corridors and open field patrols trivial. The staff's own scaling is poor until you are past 70 Intelligence, so run this as a second loadout you swap into rather than your only staff.

variants.name: Gravity Well
variants.twist: Deal physical damage with a staff, break stance, and win the fights where magic resistance is high.
variants.notes: Hold a **Meteorite Staff** in your off hand and every gravity sorcery gains 30 percent, whichever staff actually casts it. **Rock Sling** already carried you through the early game; **Meteorite of Astel** at 55 Intelligence continues the idea with 185 percent physical and 105 percent magic per meteorite, and it drops from the fight at the end of Yelough Anix Tunnel. Because gravity spells deal physical damage they land properly on magic-resistant bosses, and their stance damage sets up critical hits your other spells never will. Neither of those two can be charged, so the **Godfrey Icon** does nothing here; **Marika's Soreseal** takes the slot instead, handing you five more Mind and five more Intelligence for 15 percent more damage taken, which this package needs because it is expensive per cast.

route.text: Take Meteorite of Astel - the void beast waiting at the end of Yelough Anix Tunnel drops it.

pvp:
Duels settle at 125 and 150 by long-standing player convention rather than by any rule the game
enforces, and 125 is where a sorcerer is at their sharpest, because Intelligence 60 to 80 plus
enough Vigour to eat one greatsword is all the build really needs. Several of your multipliers are
cut against players: the **Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear** gives 12.5 percent instead of 20,
**Terra Magicus** gives 15 percent instead of 22.5, and the **Magic Scorpion Charm** swings to 8
percent more damage dealt for 15 percent more physical damage taken, which is a bad trade against
anyone who can reach you. Do not bring **Comet Azur**; the wind-up is a free backstab. Bring
**Carian Slicer** at 4 FP for the moment they get close, **Glintblade Phalanx** to punish a
roll-in, and **Ash of War: Carian Retaliation** on a small shield so an enemy caster's own spell
comes back at them as glintblades.
why:
A staff is not a weapon in the normal sense. Every glintstone staff carries a hidden number called
sorcery scaling, and each sorcery you cast is written as a percentage of that number.
**Glintstone Pebble** fires for 152 percent of your staff's sorcery scaling;
**Great Glintstone Shard** fires for 211 percent; **Comet** lands 292 percent uncharged and 365
percent if you hold the button. That means the whole build reduces to one job: raise the staff's
sorcery scaling as high as it will go, then pick the spell whose percentage fits the opening you
actually have. Intelligence is the stat that raises it, and it pays out unevenly: gains are quick
up to 18, steady up to 60, thinner from 60 to 80, and flat past 80. So 80 Intelligence is the
finish line, not a stop along the way, and every point you spend beyond it is wasted.

Which staff is best is a moving answer that changes as your Intelligence climbs. The
**Demi-Human Queen's Staff** leads while your Intelligence sits between 10 and 41, the
**Academy Glintstone Staff** leads from 41 to 68, and the **Carian Regal Scepter** leads from 68
upward, among the staves that carry no penalty. Two staves beat all of them on raw output and
charge you for the privilege. **Lusat's Glintstone Staff** reaches 413 sorcery scaling at 80
Intelligence but raises the cost of every sorcery by half, leaving you about two thirds as many
casts per flask. **Azur's Glintstone Staff** raises costs by a fifth and buys you casting speed
instead, worth 40 points of pretend Dexterity purely for animation length. Pair Azur's with the
**Radagon Icon** and its 30 more pretend points and you sit at the 70 needed for the fastest
possible cast, no matter what your real Dexterity says.

Damage boosts here multiply rather than add, which is why a sorcerer's burst looks unfair. The
**Graven-School Talisman** adds 4 percent to sorceries and the **Graven-Mass Talisman** adds 8
percent, and the two apply on top of one another rather than being added together.
The **Magic Scorpion Charm** adds 12 percent magic damage in exchange for taking 10 percent more
physical damage. The **Ritual Sword Talisman** adds 10 percent while your health bar is untouched,
which is exactly the state you are in when you open a fight from across the room.
**Terra Magicus** paints a sigil 4.2 metres across that lifts your magic damage 22.5 percent for
30 seconds, and the **Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear** in your physick flask adds 20 percent for a
full three minutes. The **Godfrey Icon** is the odd one out: its 15 percent only lands on spells
you actually charge, so it rewards **Comet**, **Glintstone Cometshard**, **Night Comet**,
**Stars of Ruin** and **Loretta's Greatbow**, and does nothing at all for a channelled beam like
**Comet Azur**.

The limiting resource is FP, the blue bar, and Mind is the stat that fills it. This is why the
route pushes Mind to the mid twenties by level 80 rather than dumping everything into
Intelligence. **Comet Azur** costs 40 FP to start and another 10 for every fraction of a second
you hold it, which no realistic Mind investment can pay for. The answer is the
**Cerulean Hidden Tear**: mixed into your physick it drops the cost of every action to zero for
ten seconds. Drink it, cast the beam, and hold. Ten seconds of an uncapped comet is enough to end
most single targets outright. Because the tear is a one-per-rest resource, treat it as an
execution button for a wall you cannot pass, not as your normal opening.

Everything above assumes you never get hit, and you will. Vigour is not optional padding for a
sorcerer; it is what converts one mistake into a survivable mistake, and 40 is where its returns
start to slow. Keep a physical answer in your memory slots too. **Rock Sling** throws three rocks
that deal physical rather than magic damage, each worth 102 percent of your staff's scaling and
9.5 points of stance damage, so it both bypasses magic-resistant enemies and staggers them into a
critical hit. That matters more than it sounds: **Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon** carries 80
magic resistance while her resistance to plain physical hits is actually negative, so the fight
that gatekeeps your best staff is one your best spells are bad at. Carry the rocks.
firstHour:
Pick Astrologer and take the Golden Seed as your keepsake; you start at level 6 with 16
Intelligence and 15 Mind, already able to cast. Let the **Grafted Scion** in the tutorial cave
kill you rather than fighting it, then read the tutorial messages on the way to
**The First Step**. Ride to the Church of Elleh, then to Waypoint Ruins east of Agheel Lake, kill
the pumpkin-headed thing in the cellar and talk to Sorceress Sellen; she is your spell supply for
the next forty levels. Spend your first few levels on Mind and Vigour rather than Intelligence,
because at this point you run out of FP long before you run out of scaling. Then take the detour
that defines the build: the trap chest in Dragon-Burnt Ruins throws you into Caelid, and a short,
terrifying walk west across the swamp gets you the **Meteorite Staff** and **Rock Sling** at a
level where nothing in Limgrave can stand up to them.

names.14000800: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon

name: The Spellblade
tagline: A katana in one hand, a glintstone staff in the other - melee that shoots.
fantasy: You close the distance like a duellist and open it again like a mage. Every swing leaves a wave of light behind it, and when a boss backs off you answer with a conjured greatsword the size of a wagon. The build never asks you to pick between the sword and the spell - the whole point is that you hold both at once.

route.text: Clear the tutorial with the starting Estoc - the Cave of Knowledge, straight down from the Stranded Graveyard where you wake up.
Buy Scholar's Armament for 3,000 runes - Sorceress Sellen, in the cellar of the Waypoint Ruins east of Agheel Lake, past a Mad Pumpkin Head.
Buy Carian Slicer for 1,500 runes - hand Sellen the Royal House Scroll first, found atop a ruined building on the hill just east of the Agheel Lake South grace.
Take the Meteorite Staff - a broken tower full of Miranda Sprouts in the southwest of the Street of Sages Ruins; the teleport chest in the Dragon-Burnt Ruins drops you nearby.
Loot Rock Sling - chest in the cellar of the same Street of Sages Ruins.
Break Margit, the Fell Omen at the Stormveil gate - he punishes greed, so poke with Carian Slicer between his combos.
Buy Ash of War: Spinning Weapon for 1,000 runes - Sorcerer Rogier, seated in the chapel partway through Stormveil Castle.
Take the castle from Godrick the Grafted - the throne room at the top of Stormveil.
Collect Rogier's Rapier - Rogier hands it over at Roundtable Hold once Godrick is dead, already at +8 and already fitted with the Glintblade Phalanx ash of war.
Grab the Carian Knight's Sword - carried by a horse-drawn carriage on the road between the Northern Liurnia Lake Shore grace and The Four Belfries.
Buy Glintblade Phalanx for 2,500 runes - the same Royal House Scroll unlocks it from Sellen, Miriel or Seluvis.
Pocket the Graven-School Talisman - an illusory bookshelf on the north wall of the room west of the Debate Parlor, then a ladder, a railing and a drop.
Take the Radagon Icon - from the Debate Parlor courtyard, round the building, over a fence, up a ladder and through a broken window to a chest.
Put down Red Wolf of Radagon in the Debate Parlor - it drops a Memory Stone, your third spell slot.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon in the Grand Library - her remembrance buys the Carian Regal Scepter, and she rebirths your character for a Larval Tear whenever the spread drifts.
Claim Moonveil - dropped by the Magma Wyrm at the bottom of Gael Tunnel, reachable from the Limgrave side entrance south of the Shack of the Rotting.
Buy the Carian Filigreed Crest for 5,000 runes - Smithing Master Iji, on the road below Caria Manor, after Blaidd or Ranni vouches for you.
Beat Royal Knight Loretta at the Royal Moongazing Grounds behind Caria Manor - she drops Loretta's Greatbow, your long-range option.
Pick up Ash of War: Carian Grandeur - on top of the standalone gate below the Royal Moongazing Grounds, reached by dropping down the southeastern cliff among the jar enemies.
Kill the scarab holding Carian Piercer - the lowest fingercreeper courtyard northeast of the Main Caria Manor Gate, beside a crystal formation.
Take the Carian Glintstone Staff - a pedestal just before the elevator on the ground floor of the Carian Study Hall, north of Jarburg.
Buy Carian Greatsword for 10,000 runes - Miriel, Pastor of Vows, the tortoise at the Church of Vows.
Farm the Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear - the Erdtree Avatar guarding the northeastern Minor Erdtree drops it alongside two sibling tears.
Trade for the Magic Scorpion Charm - give Preceptor Seluvis the Amber Starlight, and do it before Ranni receives the Fingerslayer Blade or his quest closes early.
Win the festival at Redmane Castle against Starscourge Radahn - his death opens the hole into Nokron.
Open the imp-statue chest for Mimic Tear Ashes - a Stonesword Key gets you in; the copy it summons carries your own staff and spells.
Loot Wing of Astel - from the Ainsel River Main grace go down the tunnel, take the left split past the giant ant, and follow the cliff path to a chest above a Malformed Star.
Wade the poison lake and kill Astel, Naturalborn of the Void - the lift beyond it only rises once you hold the Dark Moon Ring.
Take Adula's Moonblade from the dragon at the front door of the Cathedral of Manus Celes on the Moonlight Altar - a Carian sword sorcery that also stacks frostbite.
Light the braziers of Sellia, Town of Sorcery and take Lusat's Glintstone Staff from the chest past its boss - the strongest pure-Intelligence staff, paid for with 50 per cent higher sorcery FP.
Open the chest on top of the Albinauric Rise for the Graven-Mass Talisman - it replaces the Graven-School Talisman outright.
Take Milady - a chest in the watchtower below the Castle-Lord's Chamber grace in Castle Ensis, reached by dropping off the balcony and climbing back up.
Beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight in Castle Ensis - her remembrance trades for Rellana's Twinblade, the closest thing the DLC has to a Carian sword.
Drop the scarab carrying Ash of War: Carian Sovereignty - a roof cave southwest of the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, found by following the plateau as far south as it goes.

routeNotes.text: Early - through Stormveil, reaching about level 40
Mid - all of Liurnia, reaching about level 80
Late - the Ranni chain and the endgame, reaching about level 125

variants.name: The Carian Knight
variants.twist: Drop the katana entirely and fight with conjured swords, using a real blade only to punish openings.
variants.notes: The Carian Knight's Sword carries Carian Grandeur as a locked skill, a slow charged sweep whose damage rides entirely on your Intelligence, so it rewards the same points your sorceries want. Godfrey Icon adds 15 per cent to anything charged, which covers Carian Grandeur, a charged Carian Piercer and a charged Loretta's Greatbow all at once - but only when you actually hold the button, since the uncharged versions get nothing. Carian Regal Scepter needs 60 Intelligence and boosts moon sorceries, so it is the natural home for Rennala's Full Moon once you pass 70 Intelligence. Because the sword upgrades with Somber Smithing Stones and cannot change affinity, treat it as a fixed tool rather than an infusion project.

variants.name: The Glintblade Duelist
variants.twist: A thrusting-sword poke build that keeps a hovering wall of magic blades up at all times.
variants.notes: Glintblade Phalanx hangs five blades over your head that fire on their own when something walks into melee range, and each one lands 60 per cent of Sorcery Scaling for 300 per cent in total. You are not casting it as an attack; you are casting it as armour that hits back while you jab. Rogier's Rapier accepts affinities, so give it Magic and let Scholar's Armament sit on top for another 75 per cent of Sorcery Scaling in bonus magic damage for 90 seconds. Magic Glintblade plants a sigil that fires on a delay, which is unpleasant to time around in a duel. This is the lowest-Intelligence version of the build - 40 is plenty - so shift the difference into Vigor.

variants.name: Twin Moon Knight
variants.twist: The Shadow of the Erdtree take, where the moon-and-fire stance replaces both the katana and half your spell list.
variants.notes: Rellana's Twinblade needs 13 Strength, 16 Dexterity, 16 Intelligence and 16 Faith, so this is the one version that asks you to buy Faith you would otherwise skip - budget nine points. Its skill splits: Intelligence powers the magic sword in the right hand and Faith powers the fire sword in the left, which means an even-handed spread of 30 in each of Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence and Faith gives balanced output rather than a spike. Carian Sovereignty on Milady is the cleaner alternative if you would rather keep Faith at 6, since it applies a Carian skill to a light greatsword without touching your stat plan. Both blades are worth their weight only after Rellana falls, so run the base-game route first and treat this as a second act.

pvp:
Duel at 125 and you can afford 50 Vigor with 60 Intelligence; at 150 the extra points buy Mind and
the Intelligence to reach Ranni's Dark Moon. Carian Slicer is the honest PvP tool because it comes
out fast and cancels into a roll, while Carian Greatsword true-combos into Carian Piercer at high
cast speed, so the second hit is guaranteed once the first sweep lands. Be aware that
several boosts are cut against players: Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear drops from 20 per cent to
12.5, Terra Magicus from 22.5 to 15, and Magic Scorpion Charm's penalty gets worse, becoming an
8 per cent boost for 15 per cent extra physical damage taken. Avoid leaning on Loretta's Greatbow
and Comet Azur in duels; both telegraph long enough that any competent opponent simply walks
sideways, and the recovery hands them a free punish.
why:
Two numbers drive this build, and they are not the same number. A weapon's damage comes from its
own Attack Power, which grows from the weapon's upgrade level and from the stats it scales with.
A sorcery's damage comes from Sorcery Scaling, a hidden rating printed on whatever staff you are
holding, which grows almost entirely from Intelligence. The Spellblade is built to feed both from
one stat pool. Intelligence is the only attribute that raises your staff's Sorcery Scaling, and it
is also the attribute that Moonveil, Wing of Astel and the Carian Knight's Sword lean on hardest,
so every point you spend doubles up. Dexterity is the smaller half: it adds to the same weapons'
physical damage and it shortens cast animations, which is why the guide keeps it climbing slowly
instead of dumping it.

Carian sword sorceries are the reason the archetype exists. Carian Slicer, Carian Greatsword,
Carian Piercer and Adula's Moonblade are all magic swords conjured out of the staff, and their
damage is quoted as a percentage of Sorcery Scaling rather than as a fixed value - Carian
Greatsword lands 268 per cent of it, Carian Piercer 287 per cent uncharged and 355 per cent when
you hold the button. Because they are pure staff damage, they ignore your weapon entirely and cost
no upgrade materials. A Carian Glintstone Staff in the left hand raises that whole family by
another 15 per cent while it is merely held, so the staff never leaves your off hand even when you
are swinging steel. Carian Slicer in particular costs only 4 FP and can be thrown out immediately
after a roll, a jump or a weapon swing, which is what turns the build from "caster with a sword"
into an actual melee moveset.

Moonveil is the centrepiece because its skill, Transient Moonlight, is a drawn-sword attack that
sends a magic wave out with the blade. Stand close and the physical cut and the wave both connect
on the same target. Its Ash of War and affinity are locked and, like other Somber-upgraded unique
weapons, it will not accept a weapon buff, so Scholar's Armament belongs on your plain infusable
swords instead - the Estoc you start with, or a Magic-affinity Rogier's Rapier. Worth knowing
before you plan stats: the wiki's own scaling breakdown notes that a hybrid Intelligence and
Dexterity spread wins on raw Attack Power by roughly two per cent, while a pure-Intelligence
spread gives the Transient Moonlight projectiles about thirteen per cent more punch. This guide
splits the difference and stays Intelligence-first.

The talisman stack is multiplicative on the parts you actually use, and the parts are separate.
Graven-School Talisman and later Graven-Mass Talisman raise sorcery damage by 4 and 8 per cent, so
they help the conjured swords and do nothing for your katana. Shard of Alexander raises skill
damage by 15 per cent, which is Transient Moonlight's category, not your sorceries'. Magic Scorpion
Charm adds 12 per cent to all magic damage but hands enemies 10 per cent more physical damage
against you, and because Moonveil's Attack Power is split between physical and magic it only lifts
half the katana - it lifts a conjured greatsword in full. Radagon Icon is the quiet one: it gives
you 30 "virtual" Dexterity purely for casting speed, which is why the stat spread can stay modest
in Dexterity and still cast quickly. Carian Filigreed Crest cuts skill FP by 25 per cent, which is
what lets you spam Transient Moonlight without draining the bar. For a burst window, drink a
physick mixed with the Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear for 20 per cent magic damage over three
minutes, stand inside a Terra Magicus sigil for another 22.5 per cent, and open with a charged
Carian Piercer.
firstHour:
Pick Prisoner - level 9, 14 Intelligence and 14 Dexterity out of the gate, with a staff, an Estoc
and Magic Glintblade already equipped, which is the whole archetype in miniature. Clear the Cave of
Knowledge below the Stranded Graveyard, walk past the Grafted Scion rather than fighting it, and
surface into Limgrave. Ride to the Church of Elleh, buy nothing you cannot afford, then take the
hill just east of the Agheel Lake South grace for the Royal House Scroll and carry it to Sellen in
the Waypoint Ruins cellar - Carian Slicer for 1,500 runes is the single biggest power spike
available in the first hour. Spend your first ten or so levels on Intelligence to 20 and Vigor to
16, in that order, and put nothing at all into Faith or Arcane for the rest of the run. If you can
survive the ride, slip into Caelid through the Dragon-Burnt Ruins teleport chest and take the
Meteorite Staff, which is unupgradeable but performs like a fully reinforced staff and will carry
you for the next twenty hours.

names.14000800: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon

name: The Bulwark
tagline: Block everything, guard-counter the answer, and let the boss run out of ideas
fantasy: You walk into every fight expecting to be hit, and it stops mattering. Attacks land on the shield instead of on you, your stamina bar barely twitches, and each blocked swing sets up a counter that staggers the thing swinging at you. It is the calmest, least panicked way to play Elden Ring.

route.text: Start as a Vagabond, keep the Longsword and Heater Shield you spawn with, and leave the Cave of Knowledge past the Grafted Scion - losing that fight is the scripted outcome.

Ride to Church of Elleh for Kale's starting kit, rest at Gatefront for the map fragment, and farm the Godrick soldiers camped there for a Brass Shield - 100 physical negation and 61 guard boost for 16 Strength.
Kill the mounted Godrick Knight on the hill northeast of Warmaster's Shack for Ash of War: Golden Vow, and take a Partisan off the knight at Gatefront Ruins if the spear variant appeals.
Ride the spiritspring by the merchant at Castle Morne Rampart up to the tower south of Oridys's Rise and take the Great Turtle Shell, which has Barricade Shield built into it.
Come back to Castle Morne Rampart after dark and kill the Night's Cavalry (Weeping Peninsula) for Ash of War: Barricade Shield, the skill that halves the stamina cost of blocking.
Spend a Stonesword Key on the imp statue at Summonwater Village Outskirts and loot the cellar chest for the Green Turtle Talisman.
Fight Margit, the Fell Omen at Stormveil Main Gate with the guard up and answer his pauses with counters; he leaves behind a Talisman Pouch for another talisman slot.

Take Stormveil Castle, farm a Banished Knight's Shield from the shield-carrying knights inside, beat Godrick the Grafted at roughly level 40, then speak to Nepheli Loux there and again at the Roundtable Hold for the Arsenal Charm.
Clear the Academy of Raya Lucaria and beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon; her Rebirth ritual is how you rebuild this stat table later with a Larval Tear.
Step into the Ringleader's Evergaol and kill Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader for Black Knife Tiche, the summon that carries fights you would rather not tank alone.

Climb the ladder at Fort Faroth, drop onto the roof and work down into the rat barn for Radagon's Soreseal - it hands you 5 free points each of Vigor, Endurance, Strength and Dexterity at the cost of 15% worse negation.

Kill the Putrid Avatar (Greyoll's Dragonbarrow) at the Minor Erdtree north of Fort Faroth for the Opaline Hardtear and the Stonebarb Cracked Tear, then take the Greenburst Crystal Tear from the Putrid Avatar (Caelid) by the Smoldering Church.
Take the Bull-Goat's Talisman from the corpse left of the Runebear's room in Dragonbarrow Cave, then beat the Great Jar's three duelists further north for Great-Jar's Arsenal.
Ride the Wailing Dunes and bring down Starscourge Radahn near level 80; his fall opens Nokron and the door to the expansion.
Spend a Stonesword Key on the imp statue and take Mimic Tear Ashes from the chest behind it - it copies your kit, shield included, and blocks alongside you for 660 HP.
Buy the Crossed-Tree Towershield from the nomadic merchant at Forest-Spanning Greatbridge for 3800 runes; 71 guard boost at 30 Strength is your first real greatshield.

Open the black carriage chest east of Erdtree-Gazing Hill for the Greatshield Talisman, then loot the caravan by Road of Iniquity Side Path for the Great Stars, a great hammer that heals you on every hit and comes with Endure.
Join Volcano Manor at the Volcano Manor grace, finish its first contract, and take the letter Patches offers you afterwards.
Answer the invasion sign at Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook; beating Great Horned Tragoth drops the entire Bull-Goat Helm, Bull-Goat Armor, Bull-Goat Gauntlets and Bull-Goat Greaves set.
Kill the Tree Sentinel Duo guarding the southern gate into Capital Outskirts for the Erdtree Greatshield, worth the trip if you intend to run the Faith variant.
Beat Morgott, the Omen King on his throne platform at around level 110; his long combos are a guard-counter buffet.

Drop into the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, now open, and take the Fingerprint Stone Shield from the climbing section before Frenzied Flame Proscription - 48 Strength, 77 guard boost, and the hardest stamina wall in the game.
Grind up Flame Peak and put down the Fire Giant near level 125 to open Crumbling Farum Azula.
From Drainage Channel in Elphael, cross the roots and buttresses to the church roof and open the chest holding the Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman, a flat 20% off all physical damage.
Kill Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade to unbind the Rune of Death and burn the thorns away from the capital.

In the ash-covered capital, hug the walls south past the tree spirits and take Erdtree's Favor +2 from the corpse in the hanging root, then fight Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Hoarah Loux) at Elden Throne.
Finish the game on Radagon of the Golden Order / Elden Beast at roughly level 150, blocking Radagon's holy hammer and countering the recovery.

With Radahn and Mohg both dead, take the withered arm in the cocoon at Mohgwyn Palace, rest at Gravesite Plain, and start banking Scadutree Fragments at Three-Path Cross and Main Gate Cross - they are the expansion's real defence stat and two fragments buy each of the first levels.
Bring down one of the roaming Furnace Golems for the Deflecting Hardtear, which turns the opening frames of your guard into a deflect for five minutes.

Open the chest in the Messmer soldier camp southwest of Taylew's Ruined Forge for the Pearl Shield Talisman, then take the Two-Headed Turtle Talisman from the waterfall cave just east of Rivermouth Cave.
Push through Castle Ensis from Castle Ensis Checkpoint and beat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight to open the road up to Scadu Altus.

Answer Moore's grief with "Remain sad forever" and collect the Verdigris Greatshield along with the Verdigris Helm, Verdigris Armor, Verdigris Gauntlets and Verdigris Greaves from the cliffs north of the Church of the Crusade.
Fight Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent) at the top of the keep for the kindling that burns the Sealing Tree.
Climb to the Gate of Divinity and end the expansion on Promised Consort Radahn with your Scadutree Blessing as high as you can afford.

variants.name: The Poking Wall
variants.twist: Trade the great hammer for a spear so your damage comes out around the shield's edge instead of from behind a wind-up.
variants.notes: The Partisan asks only 15 Strength and 12 Dexterity, weighs 6.5, and its straight thrust recovers fast enough that your guard is barely down. Its Impaling Thrust skill costs 9 FP and reaches past most enemy weapons, which matters when the thing in front of you has a spear too. The Pike hits harder and reaches further at 7.5 weight but wants 14 Dexterity, one point above this table, so budget a level for it. Trading a poise talisman for stamina recovery suits this version, because you are spending stamina in small constant amounts rather than in big blocked chunks.

variants.name: Golden Retaliation
variants.twist: Spend three levels on Faith so you can carry the Erdtree Greatshield and answer sorcerers with their own projectiles.
variants.notes: The Erdtree Greatshield needs 30 Strength and 12 Faith, and at 11.5 weight it is less than half the burden of the Fingerprint Stone Shield while still blocking 100 physical and an unusually high 76 holy. Its Golden Retaliation skill costs 4 FP and throws a holy projectile back when magic hits the shield, which flips the one matchup a turtle usually loses. Running Golden Vow as an incantation rather than an ash of war frees your weapon's skill slot and buffs any summon standing near you. The trade is 69 guard boost instead of 77, so keep the Greatshield Talisman equipped to make up the stamina difference.

variants.name: Verdigris Colossus
variants.twist: The Shadow of the Erdtree endgame version - the heaviest shield and armour in the game, with a physick that rewards blocking at the last moment.
variants.notes: The Verdigris Greatshield wants 49 Strength and 28 weight, upgrades on Somber Smithing Stones, and reaches 82 guard boost at base and 90 at +10 - the highest in the game. The Verdigris Set carries 100 poise, and its pieces are a shade lighter than the Bull-Goat equivalents. The Deflecting Hardtear rewards you for guarding late rather than early, stacking guard-counter buffs up to four tiers as you keep deflecting. Add the Pearl Shield Talisman for a further 20% off non-physical damage while guarding, which is what the expansion's fire and lightning bosses are actually doing to you.

pvp:
Duel at 125 or 150 and this spread is legal at either; at 125 you will trim Endurance rather than
Vigor. Several of the build's best numbers shrink against other players - the Dragoncrest
Greatshield Talisman drops from 20% to 5%, the Opaline Hardtear from 15% to 10%, and Endure from
45% to 40% - so the shield does more of the work than the talismans do. Expect to be attacked
through the guard rather than around it: guard-breaking skills, jump attacks and grabs all beat a
raised shield, so keep Barricade Shield up in a duel and do not stand still holding block. The
Fingerprint Stone Shield's 70 madness buildup is a genuine threat with its own bash attacks, which
is the one thing a greatshield does offensively that other players actually fear.
why:
Most builds in this game are built around not being hit. This one is built around being hit in a
place that does not hurt. A shield's headline number is its physical damage negation, and a long
list of shields sit at 100.0 - the Brass Shield you can farm in the first hour is already one of
them - which means a blocked physical hit costs you no health at all. What a blocked hit does cost
is stamina, and that is what Guard Boost controls: incoming stamina damage is multiplied by
(1 - guard boost), so an attack that would drain 100 stamina drains only 39 through the Brass
Shield's 61 boost, and less again through the 77 boost of the Fingerprint Stone Shield. Getting
your guard broken is the only real failure state, so every number this build chases - Guard Boost,
Endurance, stamina-recovery talismans, the Greatshield Talisman's 20% cut to stamina damage taken
while guarding - exists to keep that bar above zero.

Blocking on its own is a stalemate, and the guard counter is how you win it. Block an attack, then
press heavy attack straight away: you get a faster, dedicated swing that does heavy stance damage,
and stance damage is the hidden bar that makes a boss drop to its knees for a critical hit. So the
loop is not "block until it is safe to attack" - it is "block, and the block is the attack". Every
swing the boss throws is a free counter offered to you. Bosses with long, greedy combos, the ones
that punish rolling players hardest, feed this build the most.

Poise is the third leg. Poise is your resistance to flinching: an attack that lands on you does
poise damage, and when your poise hits zero, you get staggered and the counter never comes out. The
practical thresholds are 51 poise, which lets you eat one ordinary attack without flinching, and
101 poise, which covers two ordinary hits or one heavy one. Heavy armor is where poise comes from,
which is why the route ends in the Bull-Goat Set - 63 units of weight and, tied with the DLC's
Verdigris Set, the highest poise total in the game. The Bull-Goat's Talisman then cuts incoming
poise damage by 25%, roughly the same as carrying a third more poise. Getting to those numbers
means carrying serious weight, and weight is governed by Endurance: under 30% of your maximum
Equip Load rolls light, 30-70% rolls medium, above 70% you roll heavy and slow, and above 100% you
cannot roll at all. This build lives in that heavy band on purpose, and only ever needs to stay
under 100%. Great-Jar's Arsenal (+19%), Arsenal Charm (+15%) and Erdtree's Favor +2 (+8% Equip
Load, plus HP and stamina) buy the headroom.

The stat spread follows from all of that. Vigor goes to 60, because HP gains fall off sharply after
40 and again after 60 - past that the points are better spent elsewhere. Endurance climbs to 51 for
stamina, which softens at 15, 30 and 50, while Equip Load keeps improving all the way to its own
soft cap at 60 if you want more armour. Strength ends at 60 because that carries every shield in
the game, including the Fingerprint Stone Shield's 48 and the DLC Verdigris Greatshield's 49, with
room to two-hand a great hammer. Mind stays low: your only FP costs are Barricade Shield at 12,
Endure at 9 and the occasional spirit summon. Damage is not this build's problem - the Great Stars
restores HP on every hit it lands, so the counters that stagger the boss also top you up, and the
Flask of Wondrous Physick (the mixable flask you fill with crystal tears) carries the Opaline
Hardtear for +15% to every kind of damage negation for three minutes, with the Stonebarb Cracked
Tear adding 30% more stance and poise damage for thirty seconds when you want a boss on its knees
right now.
firstHour:
Pick Vagabond, keep the Heater Shield on your left arm from the first minute, and get comfortable
with the rhythm of block-then-heavy-attack on the soldiers outside the Stranded Graveyard before
anything else asks it of you. Ride to the Church of Elleh, buy from Kale, take Torrent from Melina
at a grace after nightfall, then rest at Gatefront and grab the map. Farm the Godrick soldiers at
Gatefront until a Brass Shield drops - the jump from your starting shield's guard boost to 61 is
the single biggest defensive upgrade available this early, and it costs nothing. Put your first
levels into Vigor and Endurance, in that order, until you can carry your armour under 70% Equip
Load with stamina left to block with. Ignore the Tree Sentinel on the road for now; he will still
be there when your counters hit for double.
